Find out why those who die in a coastal village never arrive in the Underworld, and why the village is haunted by eidolons.
Protect those who attend the funeral of a village elder in the hills near Akros, where minotaurs have disrupted recent burials.
Investigate an alchemist who claims to have transmuted lead into gold—but who might somehow be stealing it from the Underworld.
Refute the claim of a priest of Heliod who is said to be immortal because of the sun god's blessing.
Take an aging champion of Iroas who has pledged their soul to Erebos in exchange for a glorious death on one last foray into the wild lands.

table.title: Erebos's Villains
rows: A veteran bargains with Erebos to allow him to remain in the living world as a Returned in exchange for a steady stream of mortal sacrifices.
A prominent knight of another god loses their entire family, then publicly turns to Erebos in hopes of being reunited with loved ones in the Underworld.
An acolyte convinces Erebos to bring her murdered daughter back to life, but the daughter is restored as a potent Returned who now terrorizes the polis.
A wealthy noble drives tenants out of a poor part of a polis so he can build a temple to Erebos.

The queen of a remote settlement prays to Erebos for endless treasure, and Erebos "blesses" her by turning the nearby river to liquid silver. The tyrant is delighted, but everyone else in her domain suffers.
A priest of Erebos terrorizes a village, convinced that a particular Returned has taken refuge there.

name: Erebos's Monsters
footnotes: * See chapter 6 for details about these creatures in Theros.

table.title: Erebos's Divine Schemes
rows: Erebos has captured Phenax's eidolon, the identity severed from Phenax's body when he became the first Returned, and uses it to force Phenax to serve his whims.

Erebos unleashes a deadly plague. The cure grows only in the peaceful Underworld realm of Ilysia. Mortal champions flock to Ilysia, threatening to breach the ward's sanctity and allow Erebos's influence to creep in.
Servants of Heliod find a stone that can raise the dead in both body and soul. Enraged, Erebos sends his followers to claim the stone, which Heliod's worshipers have claimed as a holy relic.

With the aid of Pharika, Erebos creates a poison capable of killing a god. Learning of this, the other gods try to force Erebos to relinquish the poison, but the god of the dead has already deployed it in the form of a sapient being. Now, champions of the gods scour the world, searching for the living weapon.

table.title: Graveyard Temple Adventures
rows: Rob a grave or the temple's vault.
Protect a grave or the temple's vault from robbery.
Destroy a seemingly endless wave of undead pouring forth from a graveyard.
Prevent the funeral of a loathed individual from being disrupted.
Find an entrance to the Underworld in the graveyard.
Reunite a Returned sentry (see chapter 6) and their ghostblade eidolon (see chapter 6).
Destroy giant spiders infesting a tomb.
Acquire death records for a family from a temple full of angry spirits.
Escape the graveyard when undead suddenly rise and overtake the complex.
Use a person's remains to raise them from the dead.

table.title: Graveyard Temple Villains
rows: A terrified Returned palamnite (see chapter 6) runs amok in the graveyard, having lost all sense of itself after finding its way back to the world.
A cyclops with a taste for rotting flesh digs up plots in the graveyard each night.
A priest removes limbs from corpses to build an congregation of flesh golems he can't control.
A gate to the Underworld releases a bloodthirsty Underworld cerberus (see chapter 6) into the graveyard.
An archmage works to raise a vengeful army from the remains of her war-ravaged village.
A mob of paranoid, inexperienced commoners hunt for Returned but end up tormenting all strangers.

table.title: Heliod's Quests
rows: Bring a shard of sunlight to a place of unending darkness.
Establish law and order in a place of anarchy and lawlessness.
Keep people safe from a natural disaster caused by the anger of another god (such as a volcano spawned by Purphoros or a tidal wave caused by Thassa).
Hunt down a notorious lawbreaker who has fled from a polis into the wilderness.
Triumph in a contest of strength or charisma to prove Heliod's superiority over the other gods.
Defeat a champion of another god (most likely Erebos, Purphoros, Phenax, or Mogis).

table.title: Heliod's Villains
rows: A local noble imposes overwhelming punishments for even minor infractions of law.
A leader persecutes an entire population of people because of a crime committed by a single member.
An assassin starts killing everyone connected to a trial after which the perpetrator was exonerated.
A fanatical priest tries to undermine the priests of other gods by outlawing their holidays.
A tyrant suppresses free expression, punishes protesters, and quashes any form of dissent.
A nervous oracle (see chapter 6) identifies the characters as a threat to the stability of the polis.

table.title: Heliod's Divine Schemes
rows: Heliod decides to confront Erebos in the Underworld. He gathers fallen heroes around him as he marches on Erebos's palace in Tizerus. Meanwhile, the sun has vanished from the sky in the mortal world, and the dead can't enter the Underworld.

Heliod grows tired of the battles between Iroas and Mogis, and he decides to end their conflict by banishing Mogis. To his surprise, both gods turn against him. The resulting conflict causes the sun to rain divine blood, producing bizarre effects.
Angry at the hubris of nobles who boast of having the best hounds, Heliod turns all dogs into wolves and monsters that kill and run wild.

Heliod arms a champion with his weapon, Khrusor, but the hero goes wild with power and tries to slay Purphoros. The repercussions border on the cataclysmic, with the champion slain, Mount Velus erupting, and the spear shattered. Only Purphoros can repair the spear, and he's hardly in the mood to do so.

table.title: Sun Temple Adventures
rows: Acquire an artifact used by a legendary hero.
Defend a hero being honored in a ceremony from an assassination attempt.
Acquire the remains of a legendary hero from the temple's crypts so the person can be resurrected.
Prevent a wedding from taking place, so the couple's union doesn't fulfill an ominous prophecy.
Expose a celebrated hero as a fraud.
Learn the sins of a person seeking religious counsel.
Find out who among a crowd of people gathered at the temple murdered a priest.
Disperse a mob of people who blame Heliod and his clergy for a long drought.
Defend the temple's worshipers from followers of Mogis assaulting the building.
Offer Heliod a burnt sacrifice to gain his blessing.
Offer Heliod a mass sacrifice to prevent him from smiting a nearby settlement.
Find a hero's firsthand account of a battle with a unique monster among the temple's records before a rival group of adventurers does.

table.title: Sun Temple Villains
rows: A once-heroic veteran seeking to regain his youthful strength tries to burn attendees at a dawn banquet as a sacrifice to Heliod.
A secret cabal of Phenax cult fanatics infiltrates the temple and uses details learned in private counseling sessions to blackmail worshipers.
An adult blue dragon, scarred by a champion of Heliod, seeks to destroy all sun temples in the hopes of bringing about everlasting night.
A corrupt oracle (see chapter 6) of Heliod sells counterfeit heroic artifacts to those he can't see as being destined for greatness.
A lazy priest of Heliod risks bringing the god's wrath down upon the entire temple.
An archmage devoted to Heliod has created a second sun, one which endlessly illuminates the land and burns those she considers wicked.

table.title: Iroas's Quests
rows: Defeat Returned bandits who are terrorizing the polis.
Defend a polis against a champion of Mogis.
Sail to a remote island to reclaim a lost weapon of great power.
Establish law and order in a place of anarchy and lawlessness.
Triumph in a contest of strength or dexterity to prove Iroas's superiority over the other gods.
Defeat a champion of another god (most likely Mogis, Phenax, or Pharika).

table.title: Iroas's Villains
rows: A knight in the polis guard regularly subjects his soldiers to extreme disciplinary techniques, leading them to start a revolt.

A general (Akroan hoplite; see chapter 6) commands a town be put to the torch for its soldiers' crimes. Followers of Phenax are actually responsible for the crimes and are framing the community so it will be destroyed and turned into a haven for the Returned.
An aging athlete (gladiator) pursues sinister magic to aid his performance at the cost of innocent lives.
The government of a polis fearful of impending war forces farmers to join a militia, precipitating a famine as crops are left untended.
A priest tries to undermine the servants of other gods by forcing them into duels and shaming them if they lose.
A gifted orator (noble) offers honest but scathing criticism of a champion of Iroas. The champion demands recompense, and the orator needs support against this threat.

table.title: Iroas's Divine Schemes
rows: Iroas inspires a brave Akroan general to travel forth with a handpicked army and confront the forces of a powerful and supposedly vulnerable minotaur warlord. The general loses despite Iroas's favor, and Akros is left exposed and poorly defended before a wave of Mogis-worshiping minotaurs.

Heliod, weary of the constant strife between Iroas and Mogis, swears an oath to destroy Mogis with a godly coalition behind him. Erebos, disgusted with Heliod's hubris, forms a group in support of Mogis. Iroas, rather than accepting Heliod's aid, launches a grand campaign of his own against his brother.

Mogis arms one of his champions with an axe capable of sundering the souls of mortal creatures. Iroas wants his champions to procure the weapon so he can lock it away in his armory and thwart his brother. Agents of Erebos also seek to recover the weapon on their master's behalf.
Iroas achieves the victory he has always pursued: he kills his brother, and the world falls into chaos.

table.title: Arena Adventures
rows: Help an unfit participant survive an athletic competition.
Convincingly lose an athletic competition so a gambler can win big.
Sabotage a star athlete's chances of winning.
Attend tryouts to become members of a chariot racing team.
Assassinate a person watching a competition before the final match ends.
Save a wrestler from a planned murder in the arena.
Capture a beast that has escaped from the stadium.
Recover a blessed trophy and award it to a contest's rightful victor.

table.title: Arena Villains
rows: A champion pankratiast (Akroan hoplite; see chapter 6) has her cronies lock everyone in the arena. She allows none to leave until a challenger defeats her.
A minotaur frees all the beasts in the amphitheater during a well-attended event.
A chariot racer (gladiator) poisons members of a rival team, causing them to fall asleep during competition.
A mage uses magic to spy on athletes' conversations and then blackmails them with the information.
A stone giant interrupts a session of games and demands a chance to compete.
A promoter forces athletes to overexert themselves, causing dangerous accidents during competitions.
An archmage enchants or polymorphs innocents, forcing them to participate in brutal contests.
A druid uses the awaken spell on beasts in the arena to make them more capable competitors.

table.title: Karametra's Quests
rows: Plant a fruit-bearing tree where one has never grown.
Save a village whose crops are failing.
Teach a settlement to defend itself from wild beasts.
Reunite an orphan with living relatives.
Convince raiders to give up their ways, settle down, found a village, and devote their lives to farming.

table.title: Karametra's Villains
rows: The head of an orphanage (commoner) believes she can care for the city's children better than their parents and works to have the other adults arrested.
A priest begins imposing restrictive lifestyle rules on a nearby population in order to "civilize" them.
A local leader (Setessan hoplite; see chapter 6) imposes harsh penalties on the poor, claiming their poverty is a sign they have invited the gods' wrath.
The head of a prominent family (noble) continues to exert abusive control over their adult children, citing their role as matriarch or patriarch to justify it.
A local leader (druid) forces marriages between widows and widowers to increase the population.
A polis leader (soldier) begins doing sweeps of the surrounding countryside to round up non-citizens and put them to work supporting the community.

name: Karametra's Monsters
footnotes: * See chapter 6 for details about these creatures in Theros.

table.title: Karametra's Divine Schemes
rows: Karametra's statues have covered their faces as if in despair, and nothing will grow. No one seems to know what has caused the god of fertility to withdraw her blessings from the world, but the problem must be solved if life is to endure.

Karametra judges that mortals have over produced and moves to cull populations. She creates new plant species that feed on mortals, while her followers act oddly, running off to join bloody revels or sacrificing each other in the fields. How many must die before balance is restored?
Karametra's civilizing influence infringes on the territory and freedom of other nature gods, and so Nylea and Pharika band together to reduce her power.

Karametra bestows her gifts on a wild cultist or minotaur champion trying to encourage her older, more bloodthirsty worship. The faith takes hold, causing the god to make vicious demands of her followers.

table.title: Watchtower Adventures
rows: Assault a watchtower, defeating the guards defending it and claiming it for a different god.
Steal military plans kept within a watchtower without alerting any of the guards inside.
Free a prisoner from a cell.
Clear out monsters than have taken over the place.
Find a spy among the soldiers stationed at a watchtower.
Train soldiers at a watchtower to face an approaching mythic monster.

table.title: Watchtower Villains
rows: A disguised abhorrent overlord (see chapter 6) convinces the soldiers in a watchtower to rise up against the officers.
A medusa takes over a watchtower and conducts experiments on the soldiers she captures.
Sirens (see the harpies entry in chapter 6) call soldiers to the top of the watchtower, then entice them over the edge so they can feast on the corpses.
A flight of griffons attacks a watchtower after soldiers steal the creatures' eggs to train the hatchlings to serve as mounts.
A cyclops attacks a watchtower, eager to devour the animals within.
A druid of Nylea, angered by the construction of a watchtower in the forest, attracts a mythic beast to the area to destroy the structure.
Blood-toll harpies (see chapter 6) take over a watchtower and light its beacon to bring more victims to the place.
A spy in a watchtower poisons the tower's food supply in advance of an upcoming attack.

table.title: Keranos's Quests
rows: Help a genius artist who had their inspiration physically stolen.
Break down a ruling structure that stifles ingenuity and creativity.
Bring together lost icons of power to create an incredible storm with the might to halt a greater threat.
Find a long-lost artifact that bestows oracular visions upon the user.
Defeat the champion of another god in a battle of wits (perhaps Phenax, Mogis, or Klothys).
Find and restore a lost art form, arcane technique, or crafting method for the glory of Keranos.

table.title: Keranos's Villains
rows: An oracle (see chapter 6) foretells disaster for a polis unless a number of innocent citizens are sacrificed.
An mage servant of Keranos enhances storms as they form, threatening the countryside.
An artist (commoner) creates incredible works of art whose subjects come to life and wreak havoc.
An archmage who controls lightning rises to power, blasting those who oppose her to smithereens.
A wild-eyed oracle (see chapter 6) points to the characters as harbingers of a coming disaster.
A living storm deluges an area, taking what it believes is righteous revenge on a community.

name: Keranos's Monsters
footnotes: * See chapter 6 for details about these creatures in Theros.

table.title: Keranos's Divine Schemes
rows: Bored with the temporary beauty of violent weather, Keranos creates a massive, self-perpetuating storm. Over time, the storm grows out of control. Keranos is delighted by his creation.

Dared by Phenax to prove that he can, Keranos inspires eight mortals with eight ingenious ways to destroy the world. As a result, a genius actor, alchemist, inventor, diver, miner, sculptor, thief, and a duplicitous goat all set forth to enact their terrible brilliance.

Keranos finds the spread of mortal knowledge inconsistent and slow. He empowers a champion to grant vast knowledge to any person or beast she touches. The advent of sagacious cattle, wolves, and children greatly disrupts (and unnerves) those who live in the areas through which Keranos's champion travels.

Keranos creates a realm of his own design amid the Dakra Isles, a place where the land and its creatures obey unique physical laws and strange truths. Some of the inhabitants escape the isle and begin infecting the rest of Theros with their alternate reality.

table.title: Oracular Conflux Adventures
rows: Race an air elemental to an oracular conflux in order to receive a prediction of the future before the elemental's whirlwind obliterates all evidence of the reading.
Defend the shrine from a worshiper who is angry with an oracle for an incorrect prediction.
Convince an oracle to give a worshiper a particular false prediction.
Help the addled victim of a lightning strike recover.
Recover sacrificial animals from a cyclops raider.
Rig tools used to predict the future so that they produce a specific outcome.
Manipulate a situation so prophesied events transpire within sight of a half-blind oracle.
Evacuate a crowded shrine during a storm when lightning strike sets the temple ablaze.
Infiltrate the shrine to determine the accuracy of a particular oracle or prediction method.
Steal a book of recorded predictions from the shrine.
Collect the materials necessary to create a revolutionary oracular device.
Protect an oracle who must deliver bad news to a worshiper who is both influential and unpredictable.

table.title: Oracular Conflux Villains
rows: A bitter oracle (see chapter 6) who has foreseen her imminent death gives false predictions to worshipers so they will share her misery.
A storm giant pretends to be an avatar of Keranos and takes over the shrine, making its worshipers his subjects.
A revenant who died due to a misinterpreted prophecy comes back for revenge against the oracle who issued it.
A cult fanatic from a rival shrine gets the temple's animals drunk on fermented fruit, throwing off their predictions.
An angry athlete (gladiator) takes the conflux's oracles hostage, demanding they alter the future after predicting his defeat in an upcoming match.
An oracle (see chapter 6) makes false predictions to convince nobles to give him money and lavish gifts.

table.title: Klothys's Quests
rows: Defeat a titan-spawned monster that has escaped the Underworld.
Destroy an undead creature terrorizing a small community.
Punish a powerful mortal for their hubris.
Reestablish the balance between nature and civilization in a particular location.
Repair the fabric of reality in a place where the mortal world was overlaid by Nyx during Xenagos's pretensions to godhood.
Defeat a champion of another god (most likely Ephara, Heliod, or Iroas).

table.title: Klothys's Villains
rows: A single-minded Nyxborn assassin of Klothys hunts a hero who was raised from the dead.
Believing in the holiness of a terrible beast, Klothys's acolytes murder heroes sent to deal with it.
Certain that civilization offends fate, a priest raises a herd of typhons to release on a city.
Insulted satyr revelers (see chapter 6) channel Klothys's magic to drive a polis's priests into embarrassing debauchery.
An oracle (see chapter 6) knows it is a character's destiny to serve Klothys. The seer manufactures tragedy for the individual to provoke this revelation.
A cult fanatic of Klothys believes that the characters' deeds mark them as servants of the titans, destined to free one of those ancient terrors.

name: Klothys's Monsters
footnotes: * See chapter 6 for details about these creatures in Theros.

table.title: Klothys's Divine Schemes
rows: Convinced that Heliod's boundless ambition will destroy Theros, Klothys creates an artifact that will destroy the sun god once he claims it as his own. She needs mortal heroes who can demonstrate the artifact's power by vanquishing Erebos's servants, and in the process stoke Heliod's envy.

Concerned by the spread of Meletian influence, Klothys fills the dreams of the polis's people with treachery. Neighbors attack neighbors, and attempts by Ephara's followers to intervene only redirect the violence toward the polis's patron.
Klothys becomes convinced that mortals giving worship to the gods distorts their proper relationship to each other, and she sets out to abolish religion.

Now that she has left the Underworld, Klothys knows it's only a matter of time until the titans escape. To prepare the world for the horrors of that inevitable conflict, she unleashes Underworld beasts into the mortal realm, trusting that the mayhem will bring forth heroes who can ultimately defeat the titans.

table.title: Abandoned Temple Condition
rows: Buried in dirt, mud, sand, or snow
Cracked into more than one piece
Floating in an unstable parallel reality

table.title: Abandoned Temple Adventures
rows: Retrieve records or a magic item left in the temple.
Demolish what's left of the temple to prevent anyone from retrieving the ancient secrets hidden inside.
Retrieve the remains of a dead humanoid from the temple.
Find a replacement for the temple's current guardian.
Consult with a hermit who lives in the temple.
Stop cultists from performing a destructive ritual in the temple.
Restore the temple to receive the patron deity's blessing.
Find a gate to the Underworld or Nyx.
Consult a demon living in the temple.
Discover why the temple was abandoned.
Restore the temple to reveal the truth hidden in its architecture.

table.title: Abandoned Temple Villains
rows: A depraved cult of Klothys captures victims on the road and brings them to the temple for ritual torture.
A hydra slumbers within an abandoned temple, having dug a lair out of one of the collapsed sections.
A medusa living in an abandoned temple grants curative aid to those who bring her a humanoid sacrifice.
A bandit captain hiding in a temple hopes to open its vault to find treasure, not knowing that a demon is trapped inside.
Blood-toll harpies make an abandoned temple their nest and devour any creatures that get too close.
A gynosphinx curious about human behavior creates a series of deadly traps in an abandoned temple and lures adventurers to the place to witness if and how they overcome its challenges.

table.title: Kruphix's Quests
rows: Seize a powerful magic item from those who would misuse it, study it, and then destroy it.
Capture a former follower of Kruphix who used secret knowledge for personal gain and deliver them to Kruphix's temple for judgment.
Suppress all knowledge of a dangerous secret, such as the location of a fountain of immortality, by any means necessary.
Bring proof of a powerful conspiracy to the leaders of a human polis while evading or defeating the agents sent to stop you.
Investigate rumors of an unearthed divine relic and decide whether it's safe to be in the mortal realm.
End a conflict between the followers of two other gods, whether by mediating, forcing a truce, or siding with the weaker group to defeat the stronger one.

table.title: Kruphix's Villains
rows: An oracle (see chapter 6) seeks to erase the memories of an entire community, reducing them to a simpler, happier, more natural state.
A gynosphinx possesses magic that can stop a rampaging monster, but refuses to share it for fear that it might be misused.
A former agent (spy) of Kruphix knows the location of an unguarded portal to the Underworld and plans to sell it to the highest bidder.
A noble sows discord among Heliod's followers, believing that the sun god is the greatest threat to harmony among the gods.
An archmage works to destroy the Temple of Mystery to further divide Nyx from the mortal world.
A cult fanatic of Kruphix learns that the characters have discovered knowledge mortals were not meant to know and works to silence them.

name: Kruphix's Monsters
footnotes: * See chapter 6 for details about these creatures in Theros.

table.title: Kruphix's Divine Schemes
rows: Shadowy forces steal a holy artifact, thought to be a part of the sun, from Heliod's followers. The priesthood blames Phenax or Erebos, but Kruphix is behind the theft. The sun stone holds a terrible secret power, and Kruphix seeks to remove it from the mortal world before it does great harm.

Kruphix sends Nyxborn to torment a community. The locals are baffled, until it's revealed that miners have impeded on a cave that underpins the nature of time. Not only are mortals not welcome there, but someone has already entered, employed the passages there, and stolen something from the past.

A philosopher in Meletis argues that the gods rely on mortals for their existence, rather than the other way around. When this idea gains adherents, Kruphix curses the polis so that no one can speak or read.
After a minor altercation between the gods, Kruphix declares a new Silence. He refuses to lift it unless the other gods agree to aid him in forcing Klothys back into the Underworld.

table.title: Temple of Mystery Adventures
rows: Find and repair one of the temple's challenges that has malfunctioned.
Seek the help of the temple's priest, who's become trapped in stasis due to a malfunctioning trap.
Solve the puzzles in a temple to claim a magic item hidden inside.
Rescue someone trapped in the temple.
Learn how a particular trap or puzzle works so it can be recreated.
Solve more challenges than a rival party of adventurers who are also in the temple.
Enter the temple and contend with a complex trap that, over time, has developed consciousness.
Lead dangerous individuals into the temple and ensure they never leave.
Question the priest to find the location of another temple of mystery.
Lead dangerous creatures into the temple to trap them there.
Defeat a cabal of mages that has claimed the temple.
Defeat a temple's challenges to get the attention of the gods.

table.title: Temple of Mystery Villains
rows: A bored androsphinx asks visitors riddles with no correct answer, then tears them apart for fun when they respond incorrectly.
A mad archmage, obsessed with a mystery she can't solve, wanders the halls of the temple and forces those she meets to confront the puzzle.
A dragon disguised as a humanoid waits in the temple's entrance and demands treasure from anyone leaving.
The priest caring for the temple gets jealous whenever adventurers solve a puzzle he couldn't and tries to kill them.
A hero challenges adventurers to solve the temple's mysteries faster than she can, but she has rigged each to ensure her victory.
A cyclops accidentally trapped in the temple goes on a rampage.

table.title: Mogis's Quests
rows: Foment a war between rival poleis.
Bring about anarchy and lawlessness in a formerly peaceful polis.
Organize disparate groups of bandits and criminals into a cohesive fighting force.
Hunt down a famous defender of the law who champions Iroas.
Triumph in a contest of strength or endurance to prove Mogis's superiority over other gods.
Defeat a champion of another god (most likely Iroas, Heliod, or Ephara).

table.title: Mogis's Villains
rows: A petty tyrant (gladiator) rules his populace through threats and intimidation. His favorite pastime is forcing unwilling subjects to fight in gladiatorial blood sports.
A band of minotaurs directed by a champion of Mogis forges a trail of devastation through the countryside.
A serial killer (assassin) stalks the streets of the polis, taking lives seemingly at random.
An oracle (see chapter 6) of Mogis marches into town and predicts doom on the populace within a fortnight.
Priests of Iroas and Heliod are being murdered by unknown assailants and their temples desecrated.
An archmage is corrupted by Mogis and begins summoning demons to savage the population.
A badly wounded caravan guard (bandit captain) accuses the characters of murder and banditry.
A cabal of Mogis's cult fanatics have almost succeeded in finding a way to summon Mogis's warhound to their service.

name: Mogis's Monsters
footnotes: * See chapter 6 for details about these creatures in Theros.

table.title: Mogis's Divine Schemes
rows: A champion of Mogis unites the minotaur bands and cyclops tribes of Phoberos under her banner, creating a terrifying army. At Mogis's command, she leads the army in an all-out assault on Akros, hoping to draw Iroas into battle and defeat him once and for all.
Mogis bargains with Pharika, convincing her to create elixirs that will turn his followers into invincible monsters. He sends his champions to fetch the necessary ingredients for her.
A bitter noble makes a pact with Mogis for power in exchange for carrying out a plot to ignite a war between Meletis and Setessa. Thousands will die unless the scheme is put to rest.

Mogis agrees to ally with three other gods against their rivals if they help him defeat Iroas. Mogis's brother does the same. Soon the entire pantheon divides along faction lines and prepare for the final war.

table.title: Canyon Shrine Adventures
rows: Survive a journey through the canyon while escorting a caravan transporting offerings to another god.
Slay a massive, blood-drunk monster that rampages through the region.
Find a band of minotaurs residing in the canyon and convince them to attack a gang of undead about to pass through on their way to attack a village.
Consult a hermit who lives in a hidden part of the canyon.
Retrieve an item buried amid the shrine's sacrifices.
Negotiate with a group of Mogis's followers.
Convince a young aristocrat who was seduced into joining a cult of Mogis to return home.
Infiltrate a cult of Mogis to learn of any raids they have planned.
Steal an egg from a griffon nest in the canyon.

table.title: Canyon Shrine Villains
rows: A minotaur captures and devours other creatures limb by limb as part of a bizarre ritual honoring Mogis.
A tribe of berserkers ride giant bats and hunt humanoids that travel through the canyon.
An adult blue dragon enslaves the inhabitants of the caves, intent on building an army to conquer a neighboring settlement.
A manticore captures warriors and forces them to fight to the death for its amusement.
A group of cyclopes capture travelers and keep them as livestock in their caves.
A lamia lures young nobles into its cult with promises of hedonism and sells those who disappoint it to other canyon inhabitants.
A vicious gynosphinx captures groups of people, then forces one person to choose which of the others should be devoured first.
The victims of the canyon's inhabitants rise as wraiths determined to end all life in the area.

table.title: Nylea's Quests
rows: Free a hydra that has been captured and imprisoned in a menagerie.
Investigate reports of unnatural horrors infesting the Nessian Wood.
Plant a golden acorn in a distant grove guarded by monsters.
Find and punish an unknown perpetrator who killed a unicorn, cut off its horn, and left its body to rot, and retrieve the horn.
Hunt a dangerous creature for a sacred feast.
Defeat a champion of another god (most likely Karametra, Heliod, or Ephara).

table.title: Nylea's Villains
rows: A Setessan hunt-leader (Setessan hoplite; see chapter 6) swears vengeance on a poacher in the Nessian Wood who turns out to be an Akroan general.
A hydra goes on a rampage at the edge of the forest. It must be dealt with, but a druid follower of Nylea will take vengeance on anyone who kills it outright.
A mage who lives in a secluded grove has been using a magic item to transform interlopers into boars. She claims that Nylea gave her this item.
A druid uses magic on fields near the border of the forest, creating animated plants to drive off farmers.
A scout has taken to hunting and eating sapient beings. What could have caused this gruesome turn?
Those who follow a mysterious green unicorn inevitably turn up dead, their bodies entangled in strangling vines.

name: Nylea's Monsters
footnotes: * See chapter 6 for details about these creatures in Theros.

table.title: Nylea's Divine Schemes
rows: When the polis of Meletis expands, clearing new land for houses and crops, Nylea decides to punish the polis and destroy it if necessary. Animated trees topple the walls, and Nyxborn beasts invade the city.
Nylea refuses to turn winter into spring unless Karametra agrees to abolish agriculture and yield all cropland back to the forest.

When tensions between Akros and Setessa peak, Nylea blames Iroas for stirring up the conflict and puts Setessa under her protection, expanding the borders of the Nessian Wood to encompass all of Setessa, creating a near-impenetrable fortress filled with dangerous creatures.

Nylea abruptly vanishes. Explorers deep in the Nessian Wood discover her sacred grove abandoned, and the giant chrysalis at its heart empty. What was in the chrysalis? Could it have harmed Nylea? Or did she leave with the creature—and if so, did she do that to protect the creature, or to protect Theros?

table.title: Forest Shrine Adventures
rows: Get permission from the shrine's druids to take part in a sacred hunt with them.
Prevent game hunters from killing a unicorn, and lead the unicorn to a shrine for shelter.
Find a scout from the shrine who has gone missing.
Escape a shrine after being captured and held there for crimes against the forest.
Rescue trophy hunters being tortured at a shrine.
Earn a druid's trust to learn a valuable secret about the forest.
Retrieve a sacred weapon held in the grove.
Recruit the help of the shrine's druids to defeat a group of poachers.
Acquire a beast companion from the shrine.
Defend the shrine from a group of harpies.

table.title: Forest Shrine Villains
rows: A group of dryads, enraged by seeing a section of forest burned, plots to destroy the shrine in order to punish the druids for failing to protect the trees.
Poachers (scouts) kill the shrine's defenders and set their traps in the surrounding forest.
The shrine stands in the path of a hydra on a destructive rampage.
A druid who lost her spouse in a hunting accident attacks any hunters who come to the shrine.
A giant boar affected by the awaken spell convinces the shrine's druids to cast the spell on other boars to strike back at a contingent of hunting nobles.
A cult fanatic of Erebos infiltrates the shrine in disguise and plans to kill all its plant life.

table.title: Pharika's Quests
rows: Concoct the antidote for a powerful affliction that resists conventional treatments.
Seek out a powerful beast whose blood has unique alchemical value.
Infiltrate the Underworld to extract a secret someone carried with them to the grave.
Track down and eliminate someone who is trying to keep a radical discovery a secret.
Assassinate an important figure whose death would catalyze one of Pharika's experiments.
Perfect a perilous ritual to awaken the landscape and learn how to discover its forgotten lore.

table.title: Pharika's Villains
rows: A druid seeds deadly herbs into a village's fields, coaxing the plants to resemble farmers' crops.
The life of a tyrant (knight) is central to one of Pharika's experiments in mortal suffering, so the god resurrects the tyrant whenever enemies kill him.

Legend tells of a hydra with alchemical lore scribed upon its bones. When an alchemist (mage) begins poisoning the beasts, Nylea sends dozens of hydras to seek revenge, catching innocents in the fray.
A town suffering from a plague seeks a cure from a cult fanatic of Pharika engaged in warlike research. The researcher's blessing alleviates the pox but leaves the survivors delusional and violent.
After the characters witness a miracle, an apothecary (mage) seeks their blood as a medicinal ingredient.
An archmage devotee of Pharika manages to shrink monsters to a size so small that they effectively behave as viruses.

name: Pharika's Monsters
footnotes: * See chapter 6 for details about these creatures in Theros.

table.title: Pharika's Divine Schemes
rows: Pharika creates a mind-controlling incense to manipulate several of Kruphix's oracles, compelling them to reveal secrets of the cosmos. Unfortunately, her mutagenic mist causes them to transform into beings they've glimpsed from beyond Theros.

Seeking to understand more about the Returned, Pharika begins granting them elixirs meant to restore their lost memories. Although this works as intended for a rare few, most of the Returned instead experience traumatic visions that drive them to violence.

Medusas the world over find themselves infected with a strange disease. They believe Pharika is collecting their souls to harvest the secrets they hoard. The medusas seek advocates to end Pharika's plague.

After losing a bet to an ambitious physician, Pharika loans the doctor her sacred kylix for one week and invites him to cure as many patients as he pleases. In that time, he cures death itself in a small town. Not only has this emboldened some of the town's scalawags to commit crimes without fear of retribution, but the news has also infuriated disciples of Erebos, Mogis, and Klothys. Meanwhile, Pharika watches with delight as too much of a good medicine inspires distress and conflict that threaten to boil over into surrounding regions.

table.title: Healing Pools Adventures
rows: Heal yourself or a diseased or injured party member in the pools.
Escort a sick or injured person to the pools.
Kill monsters taking up residence in the pools.
Capture people and creatures for the priests to use in their experiments.
Cure the pools of a contamination.
Create a poison based on notes provided to you by one of Pharika's priests and contaminate the pools.
Steal reagent-rich water from the pools.
Rescue a priest's test subject and help them undo or adapt to the transformations they underwent due to the priest's experiments.
Kill or capture an escaped beast monstrously transformed by the priest's experiments.
Retrieve materials needed to create a cure for a disease and convince a priest to help you make it.

table.title: Healing Pools Villains
rows: A group of Returned palamnites (see chapter 6) invade the pools, believing the waters' magic can restore their lost memories and mortal bodies.
Naiads (see chapter 6) guard the pools, making their own judgments about who is and isn't worthy of the pools' healing magic.
The magic waters of the pools wash out to sea and attract a dying kraken to the area.
An assassin barters captured humanoid test subjects for poison from the pools' medusa priest.
A dying veteran who was poisoned by the pools slaughters any person who is healed by the waters.
An oracle (see chapter 6) allows the pools' poisons to seep from the caves and contaminate a community.

table.title: Phenax's Quests
rows: Rob or defend a gambling parlor.
Destabilize or aid the government of the local polis.
Form or foil a heretical cult of Heliod to bring discord to the countryside.
Assassinate or protect the local magistrate who has been cracking down on Phenax worshipers.
Create a grand prank built around obfuscation and deceit to embarrass a local government or temple.
Defeat a champion of another god (most likely Heliod, Erebos, or Iroas).

table.title: Phenax's Villains
rows: A charismatic crime boss (bandit captain) unites local gangs in a bid to seize control of the polis.
A Returned palamnite (see chapter 6) wreaks havoc across the countryside in Phenax's name.
The lies of a government functionary (noble) start a trade war between struggling settlements.
Phenax cultists establish a fake cult of Ephara in a bid to start a sectarian civil war in Meletis.
An information broker (spy) holds damaging secrets about important folk and is blackmailing them.
A group of vocal iconoclasts (nobles) are fomenting social upheaval that threatens to turn to violence.
A champion (veteran) of Heliod is threatening to torch a section of the polis in her hunt for a Phenax-worshiping oath breaker.
Folk go missing then turn up with no memory of their disappearance. Phenax cult fanatics are brainwashing these souls for use as sleeper agents.

table.title: Phenax's Divine Schemes
rows: Phenax finds an artifact capable of imprisoning Athreos and engages in a shadow war with Erebos, causing pandemonium in the Underworld. As a result, droves of Returned flood the mortal world.
Phenax undertakes a plot to transform Erebos into one of the Returned. If he succeeds, the balance of life and death will be shattered.
Phenax vanishes. For a time, it's believe the god has been killed or grew bored and left Theros. In fact, though, Phenax managed to imprison another god and has since taken their place.

Phenax dispatches a powerful agent to find a lost relic called Deception's Edge, a dagger that enables the wielder to warp the minds of mortals. Once in possession of the artifact, the agent embarks on a campaign of assassination and espionage that threatens to lead to all-out war between Akros and Meletis.

table.title: Amphitheater Adventures
rows: Steal an item from an audience member.
Find evidence of a crime hidden backstage.
Defend a theater being run by a criminal cabal from a rival gang's assault.
Take the place of a group of performers on stage to impress an audience member.
Assassinate an audience member during a performance without being seen.
Serve as bodyguards for an audience member.
Find a spy among the audience members and deliver a message to that person.
Steal costumes from the theater to infiltrate a temple in disguise.
Intercept and decipher a coded message meant for someone else.

table.title: Amphitheater Villains
rows: An actor charms nobles who see him perform into surrendering their fortunes.
The wraith of a murdered actress reenacts her death every night, playing the role of the murderer and targeting a new performer in her place.
An untalented dancer (scout) poisons those with more skill in order to get ahead.
A mage playwright invites political figures to see his satires, then uses magic to make them react dramatically, which encourages more people to see his plays.
A leading lady is also an assassin for hire, and she uses a secret room in the theater as her base.
Burglars (veterans) masquerading as acrobats identify marks during their performances, then rob them afterward.
A murderer (spy) who works as a prop maker hides his weapons and victims in among pieces of the set.
A theater-loving mage uses a homunculus to spy on audience members to gain blackmail material.

table.title: Purphoros's Quests
rows: Clear out a monster-infested mine and help procure precious iron ore for a master smith.
Protect a traveling theater troupe as they perform a new play that glorifies Purphoros and makes another god look foolish.
Retrieve a sacred weapon of Purphoros that has fallen into the hands of minotaurs.
Resist the corrupt authority of a powerful priest of Heliod or a cruel village elder.
Triumph in a contest of strength or crafting to bring glory to Purphoros.
Defeat a champion of another god (most likely Heliod, Kruphix, Phenax, or Mogis).

table.title: Purphoros's Villains
rows: A cult fanatic of Purphoros turns to Mogis to enhance his craft, engaging in bloody rituals to produce exquisite cursed weapons.
An aging veteran seeks to replace her body with living bronze and enlists a genius archmage of Purphoros to aid her. Then several of their test limbs escape.
A rebel (spy) plots to set fire to a temple of Heliod and dedicate the blaze to Purphoros, driving the gods toward a conflict he's certain Purphoros will win.
A gladiator of Purphoros partakes of the fumes at Mount Velus then goes on what seems to be a rampage that contributes to a mysterious design.
A priest of Purphoros condemns the party for treating their weapons and tools poorly, insisting they discard them until the heroes prove their worthiness.
A group of oreads (see chapter 6) seeks inspiration in flames. The oreads leave Purphoros's forge and conduct thorough studies of everything they burn.

name: Purphoros's Monsters
footnotes: * See chapter 6 for details about these creatures in Theros.

table.title: Purphoros's Divine Schemes
rows: Enraged at Heliod's latest insult, Purphoros causes Mount Velus to erupt. The volcano's rage doesn't cease, though, threatening the region.
Insulted that the other gods don't appreciate his creations, Purphoros breaks the Nyx-infused chains that bind the ancient red dragon Thraxes, allowing it to go on a far-ranging rampage.

Gripped by sudden inspiration, Purphoros begins building a massive Nyx-bronze bridge that will link Mount Velus in the mortal world with Nyx itself. Every god opposes him in this effort. Can the construction effort be sabotaged without bringing the bridge tumbling down on the mortal world?

Purphoros's double, Petros, reveals an army of metal Nyxborn creatures and unleashes them against temples and settlements dedicated to other gods. The gods blame Purphoros for the attack, but he is too proud, and too fond of Petros, to stop the attacks.

table.title: Volcano Temple Adventures
rows: Acquire an item that wasn't up to Purphoros's standards before it's cast into the lava.
Defend the temple from fiery zombies emerging from tunnels connecting to a collapsed temple.
Steal a phoenix egg from the temple.
Become an apprentice to one of the priests and craft an item in the temple.
Explore a ruined temple after an eruption to make sure it is safe for others to enter.
Stop the temple priests from destroying well-crafted but substandard armor and weapons that are needed by a nearby settlement.
The volcano is erupting! Prevent it, or save the most fanatical priests who refuse to leave their forges.
Negotiate with fire giants who want to use the temple's forges.
Destroy a near-indestructible item in the volcano's forges.
Rescue an artisan lost in the temple's twisting halls.

table.title: Volcano Temple Villains
rows: An adult red dragon tries to make its nest inside the temple, attacking the artisans and priests within.
A priest of Mogis infiltrates the volcano and mars its ornate halls, hoping to draw Purphoros's ire and thus cause the volcano to erupt at an unexpected time, killing everyone in the temple.
A obsessed cult fanatic is never satisfied with her apprentices' creations and works them to death.
A unit of defeated and desperate hoplites (see chapter 6) raid the temple, steal magical weapons, and prepare to avenge their fallen companions.
An apprentice artisan summons fire elementals that he can't control to murder his cruel master.
An iron golem forged in the temple breaks free of its maker's control and goes on a killing spree.

table.title: Thassa's Quests
rows: Help a village of Thassa's faithful evacuate to the hills before Thassa sends a great wave to punish the village's willful coastal neighbors.
Phenax has learned the location of a sunken treasure in a flooded cave. Retrieve the treasure before his fortune-hunters can steal it from Thassa.

Smuggle a cargo of offerings for Thassa past harbor inspectors at Meletis, skirting new laws put into place at the behest of Heliod's priesthood that ban the import of items intended for sacrifice to other gods.
Find a magically stolen vessel sequestered high in the mountains and return it to the ocean.
Capture a great beast of the land and bring it to the shore as an offering for a kraken.
Humiliate a champion of another god (most likely Ephara, Karametra, Pharika, Iroas, or Mogis).

table.title: Thassa's Villains
rows: A triton master of waves (see chapter 6) demands ever greater sacrifices to Thassa from merchants moving along a crucial trade route, threatening to sink ships that don't comply.
A former priest of Thassa kidnaps indigents and plans to drown them as offerings to regain her favor.
A druid of Thassa, after being mistreated by a coastal community, uses magic to lure a plague of giant crabs out of the depths to take revenge.
A water elemental is trapped in a village well and has changed the drinking water to saltwater. It needs help returning to the sea.
Sirens (see the harpies entry in chapter 6) favored by Thassa take up residence in a lighthouse, preventing its use.
A ship carrying a massive pearl sacred to Thassa has been sunk. Thassa's cultists want the pearl back, but anyone trying to retrieve it find that the god's triton followers have claimed it.

name: Thassa's Monsters
footnotes: * See chapter 6 for details about these creatures in Theros.

table.title: Thassa's Divine Schemes
rows: After a kraken is sighted near an inhabited island, a fleet prepares to set sail from Meletis to face it. In retribution, Thassa pulls the ocean back from the entire coastline, stranding not only the fleet, but the fishing boats and merchant vessels that keep the polis fed and supplied. Thassa's oracles announce that "the forest of masts must be felled" before the waters will return, but Meletis refuses to give up its navy. How can Thassa be appeased?
During a divine conflict, one of the gods' weapons tumbles into the sea. Thassa refuses to return the godly weapon, claiming it as her own, much to the owner's ire.

Thassa turns a ship full of another god's champions into dolphins as punishment for setting foot on one of her holy isles. Can she be persuaded to change them back? How will the champions' patrons respond if she refuses?
When multiple gods turn against her in a dispute, Thassa is enraged. She releases the locks binding every kraken in the sea, along with that of an ancient and mysterious kraken brood mother.

table.title: Coastal Temple Adventures
rows: Save land-dwelling worshipers who became trapped inside the temple during a flood.
Steal an offering before it washes away.
Confront pirates worshiping at the temple.
Defend the temple from kraken-worshiping cultists.
Kill or drive off a hydra that has claimed the temple as its home.
Help a killer whale beached in the temple.
Kidnap a worshiper without making a scene.
Steal a magic quipper from a sacred tide pool.
Spy on a conversation between two worshipers.
Negotiate with a blue dragon that wants to claim the temple as its lair.
Escape the temple as it floods.

table.title: Coastal Temple Villains
rows: A kraken threatens to destroy the temple if worshipers don't pay tribute to the creature.
A Naiad (see chapter 6) hides inside the temple and murders fishers who worship here for their crimes against the sea.
A group of sirens (see the harpies entry in chapter 6) take over the temple and lure new victims inside to drown themselves during high tide.
A priest of Thassa falsely convinces elderly worshipers that giving more wealth to the temple increases the length of time they live.
A giant octopus under the effects of the awaken spell hunts in the temple at high tide.
A rageful triton master of waves (see chapter 6) believes everyone in a temple is secretly serving a kraken and begins murdering them.

name: Embarking on Adventure; Adventures at Sea

table.title: Adventures at Sea
rows: Slay a monster or pirates terrorizing ships at sea.
Follow an omen that leads out to sea.
Seek an artifact hidden underwater or on an island.
Find your way home after getting lost.
Find a lost temple of a god.
Relocate settlers trying to colonize an inhabited isle.
Discover a safe route through deadly waters.
Retrace the path of a hero lost at sea.
Find a whirlpool that is a passage to the Underworld.
Sail from the edge of the world into Nyx.

table.title: Island Environments
rows: Frozen. The island is magically frozen or is a floating iceberg. Perhaps something lies locked within.
Sargassum. The island is a dense layer of seaweed that has developed its own ecosystem of strange beasts and trapped sailors.
Living. The island is actually a gigantic slumbering creature—potentially unbeknown to its residents.
Mirage. Magical phenomena surround a mundane island with tempting or treacherous illusions.
Nyx Shard. The island is a manifestation of Nyx, a recreation of a land from the distant past or completely from fiction.
Idyllic. The island has beautiful weather and abundant fruit—so much so that some might consider never leaving.
Lost Ruin. The island is all that survived a calamity that destroyed a legendary city.
Gateway. The island is inherently magical, perhaps being an intrusion from a bizarre demiplane or the dream of a sleeping demigod.
Promised Land. The island is a gift from a god to a favored individual or population, specially tailored to suit their whims.
Divine Refuge. A god created this island to be a personal getaway, making it a reflection of the world as it would appear if they were in complete control.

table.title: Island Inhabitants
rows: The Last. Creatures that think they're the last of their kind—perhaps Returned, leonin, or humans—make their home on the island.
First Contact. A prosperous civilization, unconnected to the great poleis, thrives on the island.
Strangers. A species not usually connected to Theros dwells here—such as thri-kreen, yuan-ti, or another creature from the Monster Manual.
Rivals. Two settlements have turned the island into a war zone.
Prisoner. A powerful monster or dangerous figure from legend is imprisoned on this island.
Tyrant. A powerful individual built a fortress on the island, and all other residents revere them.
Fanatics. The island's residents know only one god and don't appreciate visits from heretics.
The Dead. A settlement of the Returned is located near an obscure passage to the Underworld.
Memories. Everyone on the island is Nyxborn, being the reincarnation of a lost people.
Oracle. An oracle with a reputation for accurate knowledge and prediction lives on the island.

table.title: Underwater Adventures
rows: Seek aid or advice from the eldest member of an aquatic species—such as the first dolphin.
Recover the treasure of a hero long ago devoured by a sea beast.
Carry a coastal city's gifts and diplomatic messages to an underwater community.
Calm a kraken attempting to break out of its sea lock (see chapter 6).
Make a sacrifice at a triton temple devoted to Thassa or another god.
Transform into a sea creature and infiltrate an undersea community.
Convince a hero who's fallen in love with a sea dweller to return home.
Raise a sunken city back above the waves while avoiding whatever now makes the place its home.
Seek information from an oracle who lives on a sunken island inside a giant bubble.
Seal a hole in the sea that's allowing denizens of the Underworld ward of Nerono to escape.
Return a juvenile sea monster caught in a fisher's net to its home.
Protect a priest of Thassa intent on journeying to the bottom of the sea.

table.title: Underworld Adventures
rows: In Phylias, find and bargain for information with your least favorite dead acquaintance or family member.
Smuggle the puppy of an Underworld cerberus (see chapter 6) into the mortal world.
Find and free a lost hero from the Labyrinth of Memories on Nerono.
Free a legendary lost ship and the souls aboard from the endless Nerono whirlpool they're trapped within.
Meet with your family's most legendary member in Ilysia and prove yourself worthy of their name.
Steal a legendary, long-shattered treasure from its resting place in Ilysia's Citadel of Destiny.
Seek out a long-dead foe and learn how they're keeping you from being magically resurrected.
Discover a secret from an infamous member of your family who became a typhon (see chapter 6).
Save a god's favored worshiper from a cruel punishment in the Underworld—even though they've been dead for hundreds of years.
Sever one of the massive chains of Tizerus, releasing the ancient being it binds.
Lead an immortal anvilwrought to Erebos's palace and convince the god to let the construct die.
Discover why Erebos is no longer allowing certain individuals to die.
Coerce a night hag into granting a morbid prophecy by stealing its eye.
Learn a secret way to escape the Underworld from one of the titans.
Find the lost secret of a long-dead warlord that now rests with the villain's misera.
Discover from a woe strider (see chapter 6) how to escape the bonds of destiny.
Defeat a host of legendary villains in Agonas's Stadium of Dishonor.
Prevent one of your ancestors from transforming into an eater of hope (see chapter 6).
Travel to Erebos's palace and recover a secret from one who failed to bargain for their release.
Seek out Klothys's domain and learn from her oracles how you're destined to escape the Underworld.

name: Gifts of the Gods; Remarkable Origins

table.title: Remarkable Origins
rows: The item bears the name or emblem of a lost troop of Akroan stratians (described in chapter 3).
The item is etched with a name or prayer written in Celestial (the language of the gods).
The item looks like it's been at the bottom of the sea for a hundred years but functions perfectly.
The item is wrapped in handwritten scrolls, suggesting it was once possessed by a founder of one of Meletis's philosophical schools (described in chapter 3).
The item bears a design or sculpted feature suggestive of a Returned mask.
A knotted cover or grip depicts colorful birds or stylized herd animals from the plains of Oreskos.
The item is at least partially made from the heartwood of a Setessan caryatid (described in chapter 3). The wood regularly sprouts fresh leaves, or its whorls suggest humanoid features.
The item rests among the remains of its former owner, who thanks (or curses) those who take it.
The item is at least partially made of iron.
Whoever first touches the item receives an omen from the god who watches over it (see chapter 4 for details on omens).
The item lies in a crater, as if it fell from the heavens.
The item glimmers with the stars of Nyx and is a perfect facsimile of an item used by a legendary hero.

name: Artifacts; Weapons of the Gods Adventures

table.title: Weapons of the Gods Adventures
rows: Steal a god's weapon to lay low one of that god's servants—a creature that can only be harmed by its creator's wrath.
Recover a god's weapon that has been stolen by another god's champion in an attempt to frame the weapon's owner for cruel acts.
Wrest back a god's weapon from a divine champion who needed it but refuses to return it.
Destroy a god's weapon and channel the energy released to create a new magic item or work a miracle.
Reforge a god's weapon after an incredible feat caused it to shatter.
A god's weapon has gained sentience (see "Sentient Magic Items" in chapter 7 of the Dungeon Master's Guide). Determine whether to use it, return it to its creator, or help it grow into its own being.

table.title: Nyxborn Monster Origin
rows: A god created the creature to serve as an emissary.
The creature formed as the side effect of some other divine action.
The creature escaped from the Underworld.
The creature took shape from the tales told about it.
A god made the creature to serve as a pet or mount.
The creature took shape from dreams or nightmares.

table.title: Nyxborn Traits
rows: Magic Resistance. The creature's Nyxborn nature gives it advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Light Sensitivity. A creature of the night sky, the Nyxborn has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight, while it is in bright light.
Immutable Form. The Nyxborn creature is the philosophical ideal of its kind. It is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.
Magic Weapons. The Nyxborn creature's weapon attacks are magical.
Nyx Step. The Nyxborn can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
Starlight Form. The Nyxborn glows with the soft light of the night sky, shedding dim light in a 15-foot radius.

name: Screen; Damage by Level and Severity

table.title: Improvising Damage
rows: Burned by coals, hit by a falling bookcase, pricked by a poison needle
Being struck by lightning, stumbling into a fire pit
Hit by falling rubble in a collapsing tunnel, stumbling into a vat of acid
Crushed by compacting walls, hit by whirling steel blades, wading through a lava stream
Being submerged in lava, being hit by a crashing flying fortress
Tumbling into a vortex of fire on the Elemental Plane of Fire, being crushed in the jaws of a godlike creature or a moon-sized monster
Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws

The area is dangerously worn and prone to collapse. Any impacts or damage to the structure, including from spells and other areas of effect, have a 50 percent chance of causing a collapse (see the Improvising Damage table).
Areas within the dungeon section are choked with rubble and have a 50 percent chance of being difficult terrain. Cover and hiding places are plentiful.
One dungeon hazard such as brown mold, yellow mold, or green slime is abundant.
Most of the dungeon is deserted and quiet as a tomb. Dexterity (Stealth) checks have disadvantage because any sounds stand out as unusual.
Ability checks made to break down doors, open locks, or similar breaking and entering activities have disadvantage.
The dungeon is heavily populated. Any loud noises or other attention-drawing phenomena require a check for Dungeon Encounters (see below).

A lone, powerful creature appears! You choose the creature, selecting one with a challenge rating that is 1–3 higher than the level of the player characters. The creature lives in the dungeon or is passing through, and it is hostile toward the group only if they provoke it.

Hostile creatures prowl nearby! You choose the creatures, selecting five with a challenge rating equal to the level of the player characters. These creatures are either monsters native to the dungeon or hostile explorers.
A patch of brown mold, green slime, or yellow mold lies nearby.

A group of friendly explorers crosses the player characters' path. The explorers have 2d4 goods for sale that cost 1 gp or less, which you can select from the Adventuring Gear table in the Player's Handbook.

table.title: Cover
rows: +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws against attacks and effects that originate on the opposite side of the cover
+5 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws against attacks and effects that originate on the opposite side of the cover
Can't be targeted directly by an attack or a spell

table.title: Obscured Areas
rows: Creatures have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
Dim light, patchy fog, moderate foliage
Vision is blocked; creatures are effectively blinded.

table.title: Tracking DCs
rows: Each day since the creature passed
Creature left a trail such as blood

table.title: Foraging DCs
rows: Very little, if any, food and water sources

table.title: Wilderness Encounter
rows: A lone, powerful creature appears! The DM chooses the creature, selecting one with a challenge rating that is 1-3 higher than the group's level. The creature lives in the area or is passing through, and it is hostile toward the group only if they provoke it.

Hostile creatures prowl nearby! The DM chooses the creatures, selecting five with a challenge rating equal to the group's level. These creatures are either monsters native to the area or hostile travelers
A group of friendly travelers crosses the group's path. The travelers have 2d6 goods for sale that cost 1 gp or less on the Adventuring Gear table in the Player's Handbook
The group discovers a monument. Roll on the Monuments table.
The group wanders into a strange place. Roll on the Weird Locales table.

table.title: Monuments
rows: Faces carved into a mountainside or cliff
Giant statues carved out of a mountainside or cliff
intact obelisk etched with a warning, historical lore, dedication, or religious iconography
Intact statue of a person or deity
Ruined or toppled statue of a person or deity
Great stone wall, intact, with tower fortifications spaced at one-mile intervals
Ruined or toppled circle of standing stones
Pillar carved with elemental or fey symbols

table.title: Weird Locales
rows: Dead magic zone (similar to an antimagic field)
Wild magic zone (roll on the Wild Magic Surge table in the Player's Handbook whenever a spell is cast within the zone)
Crystal cave that mystically answers questions
Ancient tree containing a trapped spirit
Battlefield where lingering fog occasionally assumes humanoid forms
A portal to another plane of existence
Giant crystal shard protruding from the ground
Wrecked ship, even if water is nowhere nearby
River ferry guided by a skeletal captain
Field of petrified soldiers or other creatures
Forest of petrified or awakened trees
Floating earth mote with a tower on it

name: Playing a Chase; Wilderness Chase Complications

table.title: Wilderness Chase Complications
rows: Your path takes you through a rough patch of brush. Make a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (your choice) to get past the brush. On failed check, the brush counts as 5feet of difficult terrain.
Uneven ground threatens to slow your progress. Make a DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check to navigate the area. On failed check, the ground counts as 10 feet of difficult terrain.
You run through a swarm of insects (see the Monster Manual For game statistics). The swarm makes an opportunity attack against you (+3 to hit; 4d4 piercing damage on a hit).

A stream, ravine, or rock bed blocks your path. Make a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (your choice) to cross the impediment. On a failed check, the impediment counts as 10 feet of difficult terrain.
Make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. Ona failed save, you are blinded by blowing sand,dirt, ash, snow,or pollen until the end of your turn. While blinded in this way, your speed is halved.

A sudden drop catches you by surprise. Make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw to navigate the impediment. On failed save, you fall 1d4 x 5 feet, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage per 10 feet fallen as normal, and land prone.

You blunder into a snare. Make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On failed save, you are caught in the snare and restrained. As an action, you or someone within 5 feet of you can make a DC 10 Strength check, freeing you on a success. The snare can also be destroyed; it has an AC of 10 and 5 hit points, and it is immune to poison and psychic damage. Complication
You are caught in a stampede of spooked animals. Make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw. Ona failed save, you are knocked about and take 1d4 bludgeoning damage and 1d4 piercing damage.
Your path takes you near a patch of razorvine. Make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or use 10 feet of movement (your choice) to avoid the razorvine. On a failed save, you take 1d10 slashing damage.

One or more creatures in the area chase after you! The DM chooses these pursuers or rolls a d8 to determine them: (1) 2 brown bears, (2) 2d4 giant toads, (3) 1d4 poisonous snakes, (4) 2d4 wolves, (5) 1 giant boar, (6) 2 dire wolves, (7) griffon, or (8) 1d12 giant rats (see the Monster Manual for the creatures' game statistics).

table.title: Escape Factors
rows: Quarry has many things to hide behind
Quarry is in a very crowded or noisy area
Quarry has few things to hide behind
Quarry is in an uncrowded or quiet area
The lead pursuer is a ranger or has proficiency in Survival

table.title: Academy Type
rows: Boarding School. Students and faculty enjoy a familial relationship on a self-contained campus.
Arcane Enclave. Drawn together by cutting-edge magical scholarship, the enclave's residents are hungry for secrets, reagents, and subjects.
Secret Monastery. Ageless secrets remain the focus of contemplation and rigorous training at this site.
Elite Institute. This cutthroat college of science or the arts accepts only the crème de la crème of society and talent.
Vault of Secrets. This conspiracy strives to keep or eradicate all knowledge of a specific truth.
Museum of Dreams. Magical communication or shared dreamscapes connect a network of wide-ranging specialists.

table.title: Academy Contact
rows: Harried Functionary. A disinterested secretary conveys written correspondence to you from an exceptionally busy or aloof senior faculty member.
Celebrated Instructor. Despite their throngs of ambitious assistants, a celebrity researcher considers you their star pupil.
Wizened Fixture. A fantastically old, believed-to-be-deceased librarian gives you assignments from the circulation desk they never leave.
Infatuated Tourist. A flirtatious visiting scholar perceives your every report and donated discovery as a personal gift.
Spectral Fragment. A haunted piece of the academy's collection compels you to complete its secret research.
Distant Observer. A mysterious sponsor encourages your research from afar to avoid alerting nefarious forces embedded within the academy's bureaucracy.

table.title: Academy Factotum Roles
rows: Acolyte, Guild Artisan, Noble, Outlander, Sage, Urchin
Acolyte, Entertainer, Folk Hero, Noble, Sage
Acolyte, Charlatan, Guild Artisan, Hermit, Sage

table.title: Academy Quests
rows: Aberrant Zoology. You undertake expeditions to document, capture, and explain beings antithetical to the natural order.
Arcanodynamics. You investigate the ways magic underpins existence, exploring its flows and seeking ways to harness its nexuses.
Forbidden History. You reveal the lost truths of the world's darkest ages, pursuing the history of purposefully hidden or taboo eras.
Cryptogeography. You search for proof of a hidden land or that the world isn't structured as commonly assumed.
Restorative Antiquarianism. You track clues leading to plundered artifacts and then restore them to their rightful owners.
Evolutionary Divinity. You dare to explore what no mortal was meant to know: the origins of divinity.

table.title: Ancient Being
rows: Elder Dragon. An ancient dragon seeks knowledge or power. It wishes to gather greater wealth for its hoard, its ambitions expanding in its advancing years.
Lich. An undead spellcaster of immense power employs your group. Its interests are strangely diverse and seemingly benign. Perhaps it's not as evil as conventional adventuring wisdom suggests?

Bound Fiend. This fiend is bound to a location, either in its true form or as a possessing spirit. Whether trapped in an unbreakable circle of binding sigils or sealed as a spirit within a gigantic statue, the fiend's influence drives your group.
Guardian Celestial. An angel or another powerful celestial takes an interest in a specific region of the Material Plane. It cultivates a network of mortal informants and agents to serve its agenda.

The Endless. This person has lived many lifetimes because they can't die—at least not permanently. No matter the cause of their demise, they return. To all appearances, they are alive and mortal, but they control the amassed resources of an immortal.

Primal Manifestation. Its existence defies mortal understanding; the being simply is. It could be a primordial force of nature awakened to self-awareness that now inhabits the landscape or an alien intellect that whispers through proxies, omens, and idols.

table.title: Ancient Being Contact
rows: Employer. An established member of local society acts as the interface between you and the patron and provides the cover of legitimate employment. They could be a bartender, shopkeeper, local official, or noble.
Back-Room Dealers. An exclusive area in an otherwise-ordinary establishment requires a password or token to gain entry. There you meet and communicate with shadowy agents of your patron.

Magical Message Drop. Magically recorded messages from your contact or your patron appear in odd places. You know to check a predetermined location, such as a crack in an ancient monolith or a specific grave, for instructions.

Visions. Your patron doesn't use intermediaries, instead speaking to you in dreams, omens, or visions. The being appears in your mind as you sleep, taking control of your dreams to deliver instructions that become difficult to ignore.

Ephemeral Echo. Your contact never physically reveals itself to you. Perhaps it is the ghost of a dead person, an entity that appears outside the flow of time, or a projected illusion of a being that never leaves your patron's hidden sanctum.
The Mouthpiece. The ancient being's voice whispers through the lips of an ordinary person. You patron might posses the body of a stranger or a party member to converse with you.

table.title: Ancient Being Operative Roles
rows: Charlatan, Entertainer, Folk Hero, Hermit, Sage
Acolyte, Entertainer, Folk Hero, Guild Artisan, Sage
Acolyte, Folk Hero, Hermit, Outlander, Soldier

table.title: Ancient Being Quests
rows: Rescue. A wayward agent went missing while gathering information or materials. You must discover their fate and recover them and their findings.
Sabotage. You must destroy an aspect of a rival's organization, either assassinating a key minion or destroying a critical object.
Artifice. Your specialized skills are instrumental to assembling components for a powerful magic ritual or object.

Treachery. A high-profile minion of another powerful figure is in a position to betray their master, to the benefit of your patron. You must convince them to defect to your organization or extract them from now-hostile territory.

Culling. A respected agent of your patron (possibly an ally or a mentor for your group) has been compromised. Perhaps they are defecting to a rival, attempting to seize the ancient being's power. Whatever the case, you must catch them to end their threat.

Astral Heist. A powerful rival of your patron stores their secrets in a mind vault on the Astral Plane. That means they can't be tricked or coerced into revealing anything, nor can their thoughts be read. You must find the vault and travel through the rival's deadly memories to find the knowledge your patron desires.

table.title: Aristocrat Types
rows: Local Lord. Convinced that power and prestige lie just around the corner, this minor lordling grasps for every opportunity to climb the ranks.
Merchant Mastermind. Reputation, wealth, and power are one and the same for the head of a family with world-spanning business holdings.
Nomadic Princeling. Nothing is more appealing to this princeling than treasure. Their sprawling merchant caravan trails behind their palanquin as far as the eye can see.
Double Dealer. The leader of a noble family has turned against their nation, secretly opposing their liege for personal gain or ethical reasons.
Ambitious Entrepreneur. The sole heir of a vast fortune, this entrepreneur seeks allies to expand their wealth in a new business on the international, global, or planar stage.
Future Ruler. This young noble is destined to rule, but currently their whims are fickle and dangerous.

table.title: Aristocrat Contact
rows: Common Contact. A servant with ambitions toward a title works as a go-between for your patron.
Professional. A level-headed advisor or manager of your patron's business directs you in keeping their reckless employer safe.
Family Peacemaker. A naive aristocrat appointed by your patron wants your assistance in keeping the peace between fractious family members, which isn't your patron's priority.
Intimate Connection. A common-born confidant or lover of your patron guides you in creating circumstances to bolster the noble family's best interests.
Outside Insider. An outcast noble favored by your patron works with you to uphold their family's interests despite their exile.
Outsider Inside. A mysterious entity manipulates a noble family's fortunes. Through your patron, it employs you to help guide its chosen family along a centuries-long course.

table.title: Aristocrat Retainer Roles
rows: Acolyte, Charlatan, Folk Hero, Hermit, Sage
Criminal, Folk Hero, Noble, Outlander, Soldier
Entertainer, Guild Artisan, Sailor, Soldier, Urchin

table.title: Aristocrat Quests
rows: Noble Union. You work within multiple noble factions to unite rival families.
Business Breakthrough. You track down and obtain a wonder your patron believes is the key to their financial fortunes.
Sabotage Rival. You break into the business or estate of an enemy noble family and undermine their political or professional ventures.
Lost Lineage. You seek evidence of a lost branch of a noble family or proof that individuals don't possess a noble pedigree.
Origin of Nobility. You reveal the secret reason why certain individuals were elevated to noble status and how they will soon fulfill their purpose.
The New Nobility. You recreate the remarkable event that granted today's noble families their special standing, enabling the rise of new nobles.

name: Types of Criminal Syndicates; Syndicate Types

table.title: Syndicate Types
rows: Thieves' Guild. A disparate convocation of thieves, spies, smugglers, and other scoundrels controls criminal activity in a region of a city.

Assassin Society. The network's livelihood is death. Members of the society hone their skills as cutthroats, poisoners, body-disposal specialists, and any other profession focused on ending lives. The society is motivated by profit or labors in service to a greater cause.

Magical Arms Dealer. The syndicate has cornered the market on deadly magical devices. They offer their services and wares for a price and acquire staggering magical might for those who meet their demands.
Pirate Fleet. This alliance of pirate captains is unified under a ruling captain or admiral and adheres to a strict code of honor. They converge only in response to an outside threat.

Body Snatchers. The syndicate consists predominantly, if not entirely, of creatures that possess or impersonate other people. They seek to replace influential individuals throughout society with members of their ranks.
Thought Thieves. These psychic criminals infiltrate their target's minds to steal secrets and disguise their existence.

table.title: Syndicate Contact
rows: Personal Mentor. This longtime member of the syndicate took you under their wing when you were young and became a parental figure.
Clever Urchin. An innocuous person, perhaps a beggar or menial laborer, knows all the right people and shares their connections with you.

Former Law Enforcement. Your contact used to be (or maybe still is) a member of local law enforcement. They have sharp insight into the law's workings in your area and a healthy dose of paranoia for that reason.
Bon Vivant. The boss of a local den of vice—whether gambling, narcotics, or other pleasures—aids you when they're not distracted by their own debauchery.
Traitor. You know your contact in the syndicate has betrayed it, but they have enough clout and leverage that you don't dare cross them—yet.
Criminal Royalty. Unknown to most, your contact is a member of local nobility or royalty. Why they maintain relations with the syndicate is a troubling mystery.

table.title: Criminal Syndicate Member Roles
rows: Criminal, Folk Hero, Noble, Outlander, Urchin
Acolyte, Charlatan, Criminal, Entertainer, Noble, Urchin
Acolyte, Charlatan, Guild Artisan, Noble, Soldier
Acolyte, Criminal, Folk Hero, Noble, Sage

table.title: Criminal Syndicate Quests
