name: Rat's Run Adventures; Rat's Run Plots

table.title: Rat's Run Plots
rows: Realizes several regular Rat's Run customers have disappeared recently. The culprit is Celia (Medium Vampire Nightbringer), who is Cazador Szarr's enemy. Celia was once a human.
Wants to hire the gnome Braig Littletoe (Small Bandit) to source a powerful magic item Astarion believes will temporarily free him from Cazador's control.

Has hired a pair of human vampire hunters named Tarena and Tali (Medium Bandit Captains) to assassinate Violet. Unfortunately, Violet has discovered this plan and has turned the vampire hunters on Astarion.

Has lured too many customers to their death, and the manager of Rat's Run has placed a bounty on Astarion. Astarion visits the tavern with the characters and doesn't know the regulars plan to kill him.

table.title: Rat's Run Managers
rows: Dwarf retired assassin's guild lieutenant; cruel

table.title: Forgotten Realms Adventures
rows: Dread March of the Bone Titan
Two Violet Fungi and a Vine Blight digesting dead sheep
A snarling Death Dog, once someone's pet, now mutated by Gaunt's serum
A Hostile pair of scabby Toughs who ate infected food they stole from a local farmer
A young family trapped in their rickety home by their beloved uncle, who's been transformed by the fertilizer into a Myconid Spore Servant
Two Goblin Bosses and one Goblin Hexer, each riding a Worg
A Bugbear Stalker and two Bugbear Warriors
Four swarms of midges (Swarms of Insects) and a swarm of giant midges (Swarm of Stirges)
Four Smoke Mephits taunt the party but flee if the characters try to begin combat.
The party attracts the attention of two Displacer Beasts that patrol the grove.
A Shadow Demon ambushes the party.
Mother Gloam discovers the party and confronts them, fleeing to the obelisk if Bloodied.
Quiet, wise herbalist; Strem's wife (Medium Commoner)
Witty, driven trainer and daughter (Medium, Lawful Good Scout)
Flighty, loyal trainer and son (Medium Werewolf)
Proud, practical father and patriarch (Medium, Lawful Neutral Noble)
Warm, sharp treasurer and matriarch (Medium, Neutral Good Noble)
Ruthless, sly trainer and patriarch (Medium Wereboar)
Affable, wayward trainer and son (Medium, Chaotic Neutral Wererat)
Calm, cruel healer and matriarch (Medium, Neutral Evil Werewolf)
Ambitious, greedy uncle (Medium, Chaotic Evil Weretiger)
One Hobgoblin Captain, eight Hobgoblin Warriors, and a Mage Apprentice looking to raid roads and settlements
A curious Young Copper Dragon named Eldiss, who knows where the Tears fell, guaranteeing success on the next day's Wisdom (Perception) checks to find them
A Giant Owl that can put the party on the right track if spoken to
Two Hill Giants, territorial and Hostile to intruders

A group working for Shar's Order of the Dark Moon who are also searching for the fallen Tears. They're led by a human priest named Alwelyn Lanta (Medium, Neutral Evil Cultist Fanatic) and a human champion named Teren Carver (Medium, Neutral Evil Gladiator). The rest of the group are human warriors (Medium, Neutral Evil Warrior Veterans).
A Wraith and six Specters assault the group's camp at midnight. The wraith's ghostly garb bears the symbol of Shar.
One Tree Blight, four Needle Blights, and one Shambling Mound entangling the remains of Sune priests and worshipers
One Vrock and one Swarm of Dretches
Three Black Puddings of Abyssal sludge
A dozen rioters (Commoners) mistake an innocent for a Shadowmaster informer and attempt vigilante justice.

A human populist agitator named Gehlen Kriska (Medium Performer Maestro), rallies the mob, blaming the city council for the crisis. If the characters defend the council or try to disperse the mob, Gehlen turns the mob's anger on the party.

Rioters have set a building on fire. Spectators watch helplessly as 1d4 victims cry for help from within the blaze. Use the Manor House map from appendix B of the Dungeon Master's Guide, scattering victims on each floor. Use the rules for an inferno in Inferno of the Dungeon Master's Guide to adjudicate the fire.
A Shadowmaster Assassin targets the characters, approaching stealthily and targeting spellcasters and other lightly armored characters first.
Your cart approaches a steep turn. Make a DC 15 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (your choice). On a failed save, the turn counts as 15 feet of Difficult Terrain for you.

Your cart hurtles toward low-hanging mining equipment. Make a DC 15 Dexterity or Constitution saving throw (your choice). On a failed save, you take 2d6 Bludgeoning damage and gain the Prone condition.
The tracks bend and swerve into a maze. Make a DC 15 Dexterity or Intelligence saving throw (your choice). On a failed save, the maze counts as 20 feet of Difficult Terrain for you.

You pass through a cavern that's home to a Swarm of Stirges, waking them from slumber. The swarm uses one of its actions to attack you, and the mass of flapping, confused creatures gives you the Blinded condition until the end of your turn.
You speed through a cavern that's home to 1d6 Piercers. One of them uses one of its actions, targeting you.
A Hook Horror notices you. Make a DC 10 Wisdom or Charisma saving throw (your choice). On a failed save, the creature joins the chase with you as its quarry.
Kissethkashaan is on the hunt. See "Kissethkashaan's Lair" below.
A band of 2d4 Kobold Warriors led by a white Half-Dragon spots the party. The group questions the characters, then retreats to warn Kissethkashaan.
A pack of four Winter Wolves led by a Dire Worg notice the party and follow, ambushing the characters when they are vulnerable.
Eight Wraiths, shades of dead Tuigan raiders, haunt the party by night.

A Hobgoblin Warlord leads a small army of 100 Hobgoblin Warriors through the High Country toward Thay, where they are to be employed as mercenaries. The warlord asks the party for news and doesn't initiate violence. If the characters fight, use the rules for mobs in chapter 3 of the Dungeon Master's Guide, dividing the hobgoblins into a number of mobs equal to the number of characters.
Two Frost Giants seek to capture Kissethkashaan. If the party agrees to help, the giants share the dragon's hoard.
Storms blow in from the west. Heavy precipitation and strong winds (see chapter 3 of the Dungeon Master's Guide ) last 1d4 days.
The party crosses paths with the Cyric cultists. See "Cyric Cultists" below.

table.title: Dale Renown
rows: All citizens of the dale are Friendly to you by default.
Merchants in the dale give you a 10 percent discount on all nonmagical wares.
Inns in the dale offer you complimentary room and board, providing you a Modest lifestyle for free.
You are given a leadership role in the dale's militia. You can call on up to three Guards to aid you on a mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
Those in the dale offering spellcasting services will cast spells up to level 3 for free (not including the cost of any Material components consumed by the spell).
The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, respected members of the dale entrust you with a random Rare magic item.
You have a place in the dale's leadership. Respected members of the dale openly provide you information about citizens, ongoing investigations, and local places.

name: Icewind Dale Terrain; Icewind Dale Travel Terrain
footnotes: *Characters' maximum pace while waterborne depends on the vehicle carrying them. †Appropriate equipment (such as a sled, skis, or snowshoes) is necessary to keep up a Fast pace in this terrain.

table.title: Ten-Towns Renown
rows: All citizens of the settlement are Friendly to you by default.
Inns in the settlement offer you complimentary room and board, providing you a Poor lifestyle for free.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, a settlement merchant gifts you 100 GP worth of adventuring gear (see the Player's Handbook and chapter 4 of Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn).

You gain the confidence of the town speaker or other powerful settlement member. You can call on said person for a minor favor, such as providing information or one piece of expensive equipment. Once you call for a favor, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
You are given a minor title, such as marshal, sheriff, or counselor. The first time your Renown Score reaches 25, the settlement leader gifts you a mundane art object worth 500 GP.
A character triggers a collapsing roof trap (see chapter 3 of the Dungeon Master's Guide).
Two Cultist Fanatics lurk out of sight to ambush the characters.
A Spy pretends to be the cult's captive to infiltrate the party.

table.title: Dougan's Warren
rows: Elder Dubrace whispering with Gutstab Grimbutcher, guarded by 2d4 Goblin Warriors
Morg watching over cousin Rogar in a cage
An empty chamber reeking of blood with names of dead captives scratched into the wall
1d4 Warrior Infantry who could be persuaded to help the characters

table.title: Genie Renown
rows: Members of the ruler's court are Friendly to you. You are provided a Comfortable lifestyle for free at the palace.
You can purchase the following kinds of adventuring gear from the ruler's contacts for half cost: Fine Clothes, Ink, Ink Pens, Paper, Parchment, Perfume, or Spyglass.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the ruler grants you a random Charm (see chapter 3 of the Dungeon Master's Guide).
Elementals other than genies within the ruler's domain are Friendly to you by default. Your lifestyle in the palace increases to Wealthy.
Genies associated with the ruler are Friendly to you by default. Your lifestyle in the palace increases to Aristocratic.
You can request the aid of a Spy Master for one mission. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until your Renown Score improves.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 50, the ruler grants you a Blessing of your choice (see chapter 3 of the Dungeon Master's Guide).

table.title: Sultana Renown
rows: Members of the sultana's court are Friendly to you. You are provided a Comfortable lifestyle for free at a lodging of the sultana's choice near the palace.
You can purchase services for half cost in Calimport.

The sultana grants you access to her palace's gardens. When you take a Bastion turn, you can issue the Harvest order to the palace gardens as if the gardens were a Garden special facility in your Bastion. Each time you issue the order, you can choose a different garden type from the Garden Types table in chapter 8 of the Dungeon Master's Guide.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 15, the sultana offers you a governmental position in the city—such as district mayor—and gifts you 1,000 GP worth of coins, gemstones, and art objects.
When you issue the Harvest order to the palace gardens, you can treat the gardens as a Greenhouse special facility instead of a Garden.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the sultana offers you a mid-level governmental position in the city and gifts you 5,000 GP worth of coins, gemstones, and art objects.
You can call on the sultana to perform a major favor, such as pardoning a minor crime. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

table.title: Oasis Encounters
rows: A Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu, a Gnoll Pack Lord, and four Gnoll Warriors
One Ghast Gravecaller and four Ghouls

table.title: Kendrick Family Renown
rows: You are welcome in the Kendrick court. The Kendrick family and members of their court are Friendly to you by default.
You have complimentary room and board in Alaron, providing you with a Comfortable lifestyle for free.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Kendrick family rewards you with 750 GP worth of gemstones.

You are given a minor noble title, and your room and board in Alaron improves to provide you a Wealthy lifestyle for free. In addition, the Kendrick family and court trust you, freely confiding information with you.
You can call on the Kendrick family for a major favor, such as a royal pardon. Once you call for a favor, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

table.title: High Lady Ordalf Renown
rows: You are welcome in Ordalf's court. Fey in Sarifal are Friendly to you by default.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 5, Ordalf gifts you a random Common magic item.
Fey on Gwynneth are Friendly to you by default.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 15, Ordalf gifts you either a random Rare magic item or a pet Blink Dog (your choice).
You can use any fairy trod located in the Moonshae Isles. Fey in the Moonshaes are Friendly to you by default.

table.title: Jarl Olfsvenn Renown
rows: You are welcome in Olfsvenn's court, and members of the court are Friendly to you by default.
You can hire hirelings from Olfsvenn's court for half cost.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, Olfsvenn rewards you with 100 GP worth of gemstones and art objects.
Norlanders in the Moonshae Isles are Friendly to you by default.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 20, Olfsvenn gifts you a Norlander Longship (see "Moonshae Vehicles" earlier in the chapter).
You can request a Norlander contingent of four Guards to help you for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

table.title: Moonshae Druids Renown
rows: Moonshae druids and their allies are Friendly to you by default.
You can purchase Potions of Healing from the druids for half cost.
Beasts in the Moonshaes are Friendly to you by default.
You can purchase Spell Scrolls containing Druid spells of level 5 or lower from the druids.
You are allowed to visit moonwells guarded by the druids and participate in their ceremonies. Plant creatures in the Moonshaes are Friendly to you by default.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the druids offer to take you to a moonwell and cast the Commune spell—contacting the Earthmother—on your behalf.
Six Goblin Warriors and a Goblin Boss (all Friendly) are having a tea party and invite the characters to join them.
A Hostile Hobgoblin Captain drills three Hostile Hobgoblin Warriors (all Hostile) on fighting techniques.
Four Hostile Bugbear Stalkers stealthily patrol the halls.
A Friendly Faerie Dragon Adult begins to follow the characters.

name: Lawkeepers Intervene; Adding to the Chase

table.title: Adding to the Chase
rows: 2d6 Warrior Veterans in the Flaming Fist

table.title: Baldur's Gate Chase Complications
rows: A cowled stranger offers you a suspiciously compelling shortcut. Make a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, you're tricked into going the wrong way, and your Speed is halved until the end of your turn.

The street was excavated in an incomplete urban-works project. Make a DC 10 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (your choice) to cross. On a failed save, you take 1d6 Bludgeoning damage and have the Prone condition.
Thieves lurk amid street performers, looking for easy targets. Make a DC 10 Intelligence or Wisdom saving throw (your choice). On a failed save, you pass the obstacle but lose 10 GP.

The Flaming Fist seeks suspects near a grisly murder scene. Make a DC 10 Dexterity or Charisma saving throw to avoid their scrutiny (your choice). On a failed save, two Warrior Veterans join the chase, pursuing you for rough questioning.

A patriar and their entourage are crossing the way. Make a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or spend 10 feet of movement to pass (your choice). On a failed save, your Speed is 0 until the end of your turn.
A spiky rune drawn under an eave pulses as you pass. Make a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw to resist its sinister influence. On a failed save, you take 4d4 Psychic damage.

table.title: Commoner Crew Renown
rows: Members of commoner crews are Friendly to you. Any crew can provide you a Modest lifestyle for free in its neighborhood and hide you from the authorities.
Crews don't charge you for services in their respective neighborhoods. You can purchase any tool for half cost in their neighborhoods.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, you gain proficiency with one Artisan's Tools set of your choice.
You can request up to four Toughs to aid you in a task. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

You are considered a leader of the crew. You can call on the crew to perform a major favor, such as busting you out of jail or smuggling goods into the city. Once you call for a favor, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

name: The Flaming Fist; Flaming Fist Renown

table.title: Flaming Fist Renown
rows: The Flaming Fist provides you a Modest lifestyle for free at the Seatower of Balduran.
The Flaming Fist doesn't arrest you unless you're plainly involved in a crime against the Flaming Fist or the Council of Four.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Flaming Fist rewards you with 500 GP worth of mundane adventuring gear (seized from criminals).
You have Advantage on any ability checks made to influence residents of the Lower City, as such residents fear the consequences if they aren't polite.
You can assign a squad of up to six Warrior Infantry to perform any task in the city that isn't overtly illegal. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, you receive a valuable piece of seized property: a random Rare magic item.
The Flaming Fist won't arrest you. The faction openly shares with you any information about ongoing investigations or secrets about significant individuals in the city.

table.title: Guild Renown
rows: The Guild offers access to a safe house and provides you a Poor lifestyle for free.
You can purchase the following kinds of tools from Guild contacts for half cost: Disguise Kit, Forgery Kit, Poisoner's Kit, or Thieves' Tools.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, you can contact a Guild agent to exchange one Common magic item for an Uncommon magic item of your choice.
Residents of the Lower City are Friendly to you by default.
You can arrange a private audience with any Guild kingpin. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, you can send a Guild detail to steal up to 1,000 GP worth of mundane adventuring gear, gemstones, or art objects.
You can request a team of up to four Spies to serve as lookouts or distractions on a mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

rows: Black coach ride in Baldur's Gate

table.title: Cult of the Dragon Renown
rows: The Cult of the Dragon provides you a Poor lifestyle for free at its hideouts.
You can hire Cult of the Dragon hirelings for half the usual cost.
You receive the honorary rank of dragonclaw. The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the cult rewards you with one random Uncommon magic item.

You receive the honorary rank of dragonwing. You can assign a squad of up to six Cultists to perform any task that doesn't directly conflict with the cult's doctrine. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
You receive the honorary rank of dragonfang. You can request the aid of one Cultist Fanatic for a mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the cult rewards you with one random Rare magic item.

You receive the honorary rank of dragonsoul. You can call in a favor to make a specific Humanoid creature "disappear" for 1d10 days. You must know the name of the target creature, but you don't need to know their location. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

You receive the honorary rank of Wearer of Purple. All cultists obey your instruction and openly provide you information. In addition, you can request an audience with the cult's inner circle. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again.

name: Marked by the Dragon; Dragonscarred Blessings

table.title: Dragonscarred Blessings
rows: You bear a facial scar in the shape of a dragon.
You have vestigial dragon horns, vestigial wings, or a vestigial tail.
Your eyes have slitted pupils and vividly colored irises.
Parts of your skin are covered in patches of reptilian scales.
A flame crackles inside your chest, and you exhale bits of ash with every breath.
You crave and can digest foods your species would normally find inedible, such as whole eggs, raw poultry, dirt, or bones.
Your hair stands on end and crackles with static electricity.

table.title: Emerald Enclave Renown
rows: You can hire Emerald Enclave hirelings for half the usual cost.
You can request a Caretaker (Scout) to accompany you on a journey and help you navigate, forage, and search. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, a Caretaker teaches you Druidic.
You can buy Common and Uncommon potions and Spell Scrolls from the Emerald Enclave.
If you or your companions are at risk of suffering from dehydration or malnutrition while within 10 miles of an enclave site, Caretakers bring you enough food and water to meet your needs.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, Caretakers provide you with 1d4 Potions of Healing (superior).
Your eyes turn bright green. Centaurs, treants, unicorns, and all Beasts are Friendly to you by default.
Members of the Emerald Enclave openly share information with you. In addition, you can request a single audience with the Three. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again.

table.title: Harper Personas
rows: Rusty Riba, a rowdy smith with a folksy accent, filthy fingernails, and a quick temper
Father Temino, a morose priest of Amaunator, Helm, Chauntea, or another well-known deity, who offers somber counsel in a monotone
Pippi Toobs, a talented but overeager busker, whose performances include whistling, sleight of hand, and foot juggling
Aargus, a humorless patriarch who's always complaining about his seven good-for-nothing kids who ran off to become adventurers
Aunt Cecilia, a silent sage, friend of animals, and inveterate winker, who's never without a bag of birdseed
Johann Overbridge, a scatterbrained rookie guard in ill-fitting armor who never has his papers in order
Vincent, a young thrill seeker and shameless heartbreaker with a fresh black eye and a cocky grin
Liza Lily, a flower seller with worried expression and a chronic cough, who looks even more pathetic than her wilted posies

table.title: Harper Renown
rows: You can stay in any Harper stronghold. While there, the Harpers provide you a Modest lifestyle for free.
You can buy Common potions and scrolls at Harper strongholds.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, you learn one persona from the Harper Personas table.
You receive a 15 percent discount when you buy potions, scrolls, and adventuring gear at Harper strongholds.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 25, you receive a Harper Pin (silver) and learn an additional persona from the Harper Personas table.
When you enter a settlement for the first time, local Harpers freely share any notable rumors and important intel with you.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 40, you receive a Harper Pin (golden) and learn an additional persona from the Harper Personas table.
You can request a single audience with the High Harpers. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again.

table.title: Lords' Alliance Renown
rows: Nobles from Amphail, Daggerford, and Yartar are Friendly to you by default.

While in an alliance settlement whose nobles are Friendly to you by default, you can buy potions and Spell Scrolls from an alliance quartermaster at a 10 percent discount. A Spell Scroll bought with this discount can contain a spell of level 3 or lower.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, your lord gives you one random Uncommon magic item.
Nobles from Longsaddle, Mirabar, and Neverwinter are Friendly to you by default.
In any Lords' Alliance settlement, you can enlist a spellcaster to cast the Sending spell for you at no charge, targeting an alliance representative.
Nobles from Baldur's Gate, Mithral Hall, Silverymoon, and Waterdeep are Friendly to you by default.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 40, your lord gives you one random Rare magic item.

You can request an audience with any representative of the Lords' Alliance. In addition, you can request a detail of up to three Knights to accompany you for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

table.title: Order of the Gauntlet Renown
rows: You can stay freely at any chapter of the Order of the Gauntlet, which provides you with a Modest lifestyle.
You earn the honorary title of knight of the guard. Patrons and priests of any temple or shrine of Helm, Hoar, Tor, or Tyr are Friendly to you by default.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the order gifts you one random Uncommon magic item from the Armor, Ring, or Weapon category.
You earn the honorary title of knight of the banner. Spellcasters at any temple or shrine at which priests are Friendly to you by default and will cast spells of level 2 or lower for you for free.

When you visit a temple at which priests are Friendly to you by default, you can enlist 1d4 Knights to aid you for 10 days. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

You earn the honorary title of knight of justice. Patrons and priests of any temple, shrine, or other established presence of a deity associated with a good-aligned plane of existence are Friendly to you by default.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 40, the order gifts you one random Rare magic item from the Armor, Ring, or Weapon category.

You earn the honorary title of chapter knight. If you or one of your allies dies and the body is brought to a temple at which priests are Friendly to you by default, agents of the order cast the Resurrection spell, targeting the deceased. This reward is free the first time you use it. On subsequent occasions, you must provide any Material components normally consumed by the spell.

name: Renown Rewards; Purple Dragon Knights Renown

table.title: Purple Dragon Knights Renown
rows: The Purple Dragon Knights provide you a Comfortable lifestyle for free at Purplemont, the faction's fortress in Suzail.
You can hire Cormyrean hirelings for half the usual cost.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Purple Dragon Knights give you an Uncommon magic item from the Armor or Weapon category.
You are given an honorary Cormyrean knighthood. The royal family of Cormyr is Friendly to you by default.
Amethyst dragons are Friendly to you by default.

You can command a troop of 1d6 Knights to help you on a mission or complete one task that doesn't go against the Purple Dragon Knights' core principles. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
You are trusted by the Purple Dragon Knights' Great Knight, who confides in you and provides information.

You are asked to take care of an amethyst dragon egg until it hatches. Additionally, you can call on a High Knight to perform a major favor for you, such as granting a private audience with the royal family. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

table.title: Amethyst Dragon Quests
rows: "Destroy a cell of the Cult of the Dragon, and bring me the cult leader's head."
"Find a lance that befits my majesty."
"Travel to another world. Return to me only once you have something worth showing."
"A psychic disturbance pains me. Locate the monster causing this, and slay it."
"I yearn to see an aerie atop a mountain of unparalleled beauty. Take this amethyst to such a place."
"I sense the presence of a wayward flumph somewhere on this world. Help this flumph find its cloister."

table.title: Red Wizards Renown
rows: You know the locations of Thayan enclaves around Faerûn and can enter and stay in them, providing you a Comfortable lifestyle for free.
You can buy the following kinds of adventuring gear from Thayan merchants at half cost: Arcane Focus, Ink, Ink Pen, Paper, Parchment, Potion of Healing, and Spell Scroll (cantrip or level 1).
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Red Wizards give you an Uncommon magic item from the Rod, Staff, or Wand category.
You have Advantage on ability checks made to influence a creature while bartering to buy or sell a magic item.
You gain access to a tattoo artist who can ink Thayan Spell Tattoos on your body (see "Tattoo Magic" below).
The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the Red Wizards give you a Rare magic item from the Rod, Staff, Wand, or Wondrous Item category.

When preparing to cast a Circle spell (see chapter 5) in a town or larger settlement, you can recruit 1d4 Mages to assist you for free. The mages arrive in 1d10 days. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 50, the Red Wizards give you a Very Rare magic item from the Rod, Staff, Wand, or Wondrous Item category.

table.title: Zhentarim Renown
rows: You earn the honorary title of fang. You can stay in Zhentarim-controlled safe houses and inns, providing you a Poor lifestyle for free.
You can reliably sell stolen goods in settlements.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, you receive a random Uncommon magic item.
You earn the honorary title of wolf. You receive a 10% discount when buying weapons, armor, and adventuring gear in Zhentarim-controlled markets.
You earn the honorary title of viper. In Zhentarim-controlled settlements, you have Advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks made to influence others.

You can assign a group of up to six Spies to complete a task that doesn't interfere with the Zhentarim's business. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. In addition, the first time your Renown Score reaches 30, an ardragon gives you a writ for a Zhentarim insignia (see "Zhentarim Insignias" below).

You earn the honorary title of ardragon and receive the authority and funds necessary to establish your own Zhentarim outpost. In addition, you can call on a Zhentarim-allied Beholder for help on a single mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again.
You earn the honorary title of dread lord. In addition, the first time your Renown Score reaches 50, Zhentarim agents cast the Clone spell, targeting you, for free.

name: Severe Temporal Effects; Weird Time Gate Effects

table.title: Weird Time Gate Effects
rows: Extreme Weather. The area has one environmental effect: extreme cold, extreme heat, heavy precipitation, or strong wind (see the Dungeon Master's Guide for details about each).
Dulled or Warped Magic. The area is a dead magic zone or wild magic zone (see the Dungeon Master's Guide for details about both). The presence of either zone doesn't affect the time gate.
Fast Movement. All creatures' Speeds are doubled.
Slow Movement. All creatures' Speeds are halved (round down).

table.title: Fool's Needle Gate Creatures
rows: The remains of an overzealous Netherese mage, this creature is enraged and confused after accidentally floating through the time gate.
The result of irresponsible summoning, these aggressive creatures wreaked havoc in Eileanar until their summoner accidentally shoved them through the time gate.
A magical bodyguard to a low-ranking mage, this creature wandered through the time gate and thinks the characters threaten its creator.
This magical experiment gone awry doesn't seem to know or care that it wandered through the time gate; it wants only to destroy everything it can.
This dangerous magical storm originated in Eileanar and now rampages on Fool's Needle.
This confused Netherese servant took a wrong turn on the way to a party; it's convinced the characters have killed its master.

name: A Bloody Scene; Forgotten Chamber Gate Creatures

table.title: Forgotten Chamber Gate Creatures
rows: Unaware of the time gate, this yeti lives in the caldera and defends it from intruders.
This confused predator wandered through the portal from a nearby mining tunnel in Conch.
The remnants of a High Netherese shift commander who was poisoned by her workers, this furious Undead assumes the characters are responsible for her death.
This obstinate creature was indiscriminately killing miners when it accidentally wandered through the portal.
High Netherese mages released this creature into Conch's mines to punish disobedient miners, but it mistakenly trudged through the portal.
This oblivious creature wants to build a nest in the chasm that holds the portal.
This creature gorged itself on trash from Conch's mining tunnels before accidentally lumbering through the portal.
A scout for a larger band of trolls, this creature wants to clear the caldera of all threats before its companions move in.
An ash tree dedicated to defending the forest's people in Lorwyn or the forest's trees in Shadowmoor.
A black poplar tree that loves to contemplate philosophy.
A rowan tree that seeks to destroy all technology.
A yew tree of a variety so rare that they're rumored to be extinct.

name: Special Facilities

table.title: Special Facilities
rows: Ability to use Artisan's Tools as a Spellcasting Focus
Ability to use a Spellcasting Focus
Ability to use Artisan's Tools as a Spellcasting Focus

footnotes: *Certain benefits of this facility have additional prerequisites.

table.title: Party Makeup
rows: One-House Party. Choose a dragonmarked house and connect all characters to it.
Bodyguards. A Deneith Fighter, a Jorasco Cleric, a Medani Wizard, and a Phiarlan Monk are assigned to protect important people.
Bounty Hunters. A Sivis Bard, a Tharashk Barbarian, a Tharashk Ranger, and a Vadalis Druid venture into the wild to pursue fugitives.
Dragonshard Prospectors. House Tharashk leads a dragonshard-mining expedition, sending a Druid and a Ranger accompanied by a Lyrandar Sorcerer and a Thuranni Bard.
Lawkeepers. A Deneith Fighter, a Deneith Paladin, a Lyrandar Sorcerer, and a Medani Rogue enforce the law—particularly the terms of the Treaty of Thronehold, which governs international law.

Medical Extraction Team. A Cannith Artificer, a Deneith Paladin, a Jorasco Cleric, and a Thuranni Monk venture into war zones and disaster areas to protect civilians, heal them, and escort them away from danger.
Researchers. A Cannith Artificer, a Deneith Paladin, a Medani Rogue (Arcane Trickster), and a Sivis Wizard carry out arcane research for the Twelve.
Strike Force. A Cannith Artificer, a Deneith Fighter, a Jorasco Cleric, and a Thuranni Rogue strike hard and fast against enemies of the dragonmarked houses or the Five Nations as a whole.

table.title: House Intrigue
rows: Dragonmarked houses vie for influence over a prominent individual (perhaps one of the characters).
Dragonmarked houses compete for control of a key site.
Tension builds between two rival dragonmarked houses, threatening to erupt into a deadly feud.
Villains from two or more dragonmarked houses form a dangerous alliance.
A villain tries to disrupt an alliance between two or more dragonmarked houses.
Splinter factions from two dragonmarked houses try toform a new house.

table.title: Age of Demons Finds
rows: A statuette of a demonic frog-like figure made of an unknown, slimy substance
A dagger with a jagged blade whose handle squirms when held
A jeweled box that screams when opened
A circlet or necklace with prongs that bite into the skin when it's worn
A plain metal ring that causes its wearer to hear incessant, unintelligible whispers
An amulet or figurine covered with a sickly-looking lichen that feels cold to the touch
A piece of jewelry set with a translucent gemstone; an indistinct shape inside the gem moves at random
A weapon made from dark metal that dims the light immediately surrounding it
A die made of petrified bone with mysterious glyphs on the faces
Glass bangles of shifting colors that make no sound striking against each other
A metal scepter topped with a monstrous head much denser than the rest of the scepter, which makes it unbalanced
A medallion or sculpture depicting a Fiend locked in battle with a Celestial or Dragon

name: Trek to the Temple; Jungle Mishaps

table.title: Jungle Mishaps
rows: One Vulkoori Venom Priest and two Vulkoori Stingblades
Three Vulkoori Stingblades and one Giant Scorpion
One Scout Captain, one Vulkoori Venom Priest, and four Vulkoori Stingblades (all drow) just starting a battle against the party's rivals

table.title: Crash Damage
headers: Size of Creature or Object Struck

table.title: Environmental Hazards
rows: The airship experiences rough turbulence. Each creature aboard the ship must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or have the Poisoned condition for 1d4 hours due to motion sickness.

The airship travels at extreme altitudes for 1d4 hours. During this time, the ship is in an area of extreme cold (see "Extreme Cold" in the Dungeon Master's Guide) and reduced gravity: creatures' and objects' weights are halved, and creatures' High Jump and Long Jump distances are doubled.

The airship passes through a lightning storm, which takes 1d4 hours. During this time, the area around the ship is Heavily Obscured, and any creature that starts its turn on the ship's deck must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or be struck by lightning and take 4 (1d8) Lightning damage.

The airship enters an area of strong wind (see "Strong Wind" in the Dungeon Master's Guide), which lasts for 1d4 hours. When the ship first enters this area, the crew member operating the ship's Helm must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, or the ship inverts.

table.title: Wild Magic
rows: Shadowy tendrils lash around you. Each creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 1d12 necrotic damage. You also gain 1d12 temporary hit points.
You teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Until your rage ends, you can use this effect again on each of your turns as a bonus action.

An intangible spirit, which looks like a flumph or a pixie (your choice), appears within 5 feet of one creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you. At the end of the current turn, the spirit explodes, and each creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d6 force damage. Until your rage ends, you can use this effect again, summoning another spirit, on each of your turns as a bonus action.

Magic infuses one weapon of your choice that you are holding. Until your rage ends, the weapon's damage type changes to force, and it gains the light and thrown properties, with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. If the weapon leaves your hand, the weapon reappears in your hand at the end of the current turn.
Whenever a creature hits you with an attack roll before your rage ends, that creature takes 1d6 force damage, as magic lashes out in retribution.
Until your rage ends, you are surrounded by multi colored, protective lights; you gain a +1 bonus to AC, and while within 10 feet of you, your allies gain the same bonus.
Flowers and vines temporarily grow around you. Until your rage ends, the ground within 15 feet of you is difficult terrain for your enemies.

A bolt of light shoots from your chest. Another creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 1d6 radiant damage and be blinded until the start of your next turn. Until your rage ends, you can use this effect again on each of your turns as a bonus action.

table.title: Spirit Tales
rows: Tale of the Clever Animal. For the next 10 minutes, whenever the target makes an Intelligence, a Wisdom, or a Charisma check, the target can roll an extra die immediately after rolling the d20 and add the extra die's number to the check. The extra die is the same type as your Bardic Inspiration die.
Tale of the Renowned Duelist. You make a melee spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes force damage equal to two rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die + your Charisma modifier.

Tale of the Beloved Friends. The target and another creature of its choice it can see within 5 feet of it gains temporary hit points equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die + your Charisma modifier.

Tale of the Runaway. The target can immediately use its reaction to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. When the target teleports, it can choose a number of creatures it can see within 30 feet of it up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 0) to immediately use the same reaction.
Tale of the Avenger. For 1 minute, any creature that hits the target with a melee attack takes force damage equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die.

Tale of the Traveler. The target gains temporary hit points equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die + your bard level. While it has these temporary hit points, the target's walking speed increases by 10 feet and it gains a +1 bonus to its AC.

Tale of the Beguiler. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take psychic damage equal to two rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die, and the target is incapacitated until the end of its next turn.

Tale of the Phantom. The target becomes invisible until the end of its next turn or until it hits a creature with an attack. If the target hits a creature with an attack during this invisibility, the creature it hits takes necrotic damage equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die and is frightened of the target until the end of the frightened creature's next turn.

Tale of the Brute. Each creature of the target's choice it can see within 30 feet of it must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes thunder damage equal to three rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die and is knocked prone. A creature that succeeds on its saving throw takes half as much damage and isn't knocked prone.

Tale of the Dragon. The target spews fire from the mouth in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking fire damage equal to four rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Tale of the Angel. The target regains hit points equal to two rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die + your Charisma modifier, and you end one condition from the following list affecting the target: blinded, deafened, paralyzed, petrified, or poisoned.

Tale of the Mind-Bender. You evoke an incomprehensible fable from an otherworldly being. The target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or take psychic damage equal to three rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die and be stunned until the end of its next turn.

table.title: Wild Magic Surge
rows: Roll on this table at the start of each of your turns for the next minute, ignoring this result on subsequent rolls.
For the next minute, you can see any invisible creature if you have line of sight to it.
A modron chosen and controlled by the DM appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you, then disappears 1 minute later.
You cast fireball as a 3rd-level spell centered on yourself.
You cast magic missile as a 5th-level spell.
Roll a d10. Your height changes by a number of inches equal to the roll. If the roll is odd, you shrink. If the roll is even, you grow.
You cast confusion centered on yourself.
For the next minute, you regain 5 hit points at the start of each of your turns.
You grow a long beard made of feathers that remains until you sneeze, at which point the feathers explode out from your face.
You cast grease centered on yourself.
Creatures have disadvantage on saving throws against the next spell you cast in the next minute that involves a saving throw.
Your skin turns a vibrant shade of blue. A remove curse spell can end this effect.
An eye appears on your forehead for the next minute. During that time, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
For the next minute, all your spells with a casting time of 1 action have a casting time of 1 bonus action.
You teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see.
You are transported to the Astral Plane until the end of your next turn, after which time you return to the space you previously occupied or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.
Maximize the damage of the next damaging spell you cast within the next minute.
Roll a d10. Your age changes by a number of years equal to the roll. If the roll is odd, you get younger (minimum 1 year old). If the roll is even, you get older.
1d6 flumphs controlled by the DM appear in unoccupied spaces within 60 feet of you and are frightened of you. They vanish after 1 minute.

You turn into a potted plant until the start of your next turn. While a plant, you are incapacitated and have vulnerability to all damage. If you drop to 0 hit points, your pot breaks, and your form reverts.
For the next minute, you can teleport up to 20 feet as a bonus action on each of your turns.
A unicorn controlled by the DM appears in a space within 5 feet of you, then disappears 1 minute later.
You can't speak for the next minute. Whenever you try, pink bubbles float out of your mouth.
A spectral shield hovers near you for the next minute, granting you a +2 bonus to AC and immunity to magic missile.
You are immune to being intoxicated by alcohol for the next 5d6 days.
Your hair falls out but grows back within 24 hours.
For the next minute, any flammable object you touch that isn't being worn or carried by another creature bursts into flame.
You regain your lowest-level expended spell slot.
For the next minute, you must shout when you speak.
You cast fog cloud centered on yourself.
Up to three creatures you choose within 30 feet of you take 4d10 lightning damage.
You are frightened by the nearest creature until the end of your next turn.
Each creature within 30 feet of you becomes invisible for the next minute. The invisibility ends on a creature when it attacks or casts a spell.
You gain resistance to all damage for the next minute.
A random creature within 60 feet of you becomes poisoned for 1d4 hours.
You glow with bright light in a 30-foot radius for the next minute. Any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of you is blinded until the end of its next turn.
You cast polymorph on yourself. If you fail the saving throw, you turn into a sheep for the spell's duration.
Illusory butterflies and flower petals flutter in the air within 10 feet of you for the next minute.
You can take one additional action immediately.
Each creature within 30 feet of you takes 1d10 necrotic damage. You regain hit points equal to the sum of the necrotic damage dealt.
You cast fly on a random creature within 60 feet of you.
You become invisible for the next minute. During that time, other creatures can't hear you. The invisibility ends if you attack or cast a spell.
If you die within the next minute, you immediately come back to life as if by the reincarnate spell.
Your size increases by one size category for the next minute.
You and all creatures within 30 feet of you gain vulnerability to piercing damage for the next minute.
You are surrounded by faint, ethereal music for the next minute.
You regain all expended sorcery points.

table.title: Wild Magic Surge
rows: Roll on this table at the start of each of your turns for the next minute, ignoring this result on subsequent rolls.

A creature that is Friendly toward you appears in a random unoccupied space within 60 feet of you. The creature is under the DM's control and disappears 1 minute later. Roll 1d4 to determine the creature: on a 1, a Modron Duodrone appears; on a 2, a Flumph appears; on a 3, a Modron Monodrone appears; on a 4, a Unicorn appears. See the Monster Manual for the creature's stat block.
For the next minute, you regain 5 Hit Points at the start of each of your turns.
Creatures have Disadvantage on saving throws against the next spell you cast in the next minute that involves a saving throw.

You are subjected to an effect that lasts for 1 minute unless its description says otherwise. Roll 1d8 to determine the effect: on a 1, you're surrounded by faint, ethereal music only you and creatures within 5 feet of you can hear; on a 2, your size increases by one size category; on a 3, you grow a long beard made of feathers that remains until you sneeze, at which point the feathers explode from your face and vanish; on a 4, you must shout when you speak; on a 5, illusory butterflies flutter in the air within 10 feet of you; on a 6, an eye appears on your forehead, granting you Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks; on an 7, pink bubbles float out of your mouth whenever you speak; on an 8, your skin turns a vibrant shade of blue for 24 hours or until the effect is ended by a Remove Curse spell.
For the next minute, all your spells with a casting time of an action have a casting time of a Bonus Action.
You are transported to the Astral Plane until the end of your next turn. You then return to the space you previously occupied or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.
The next time you cast a spell that deals damage within the next minute, don't roll the spell's damage dice for the damage. Instead use the highest number possible for each damage die.
You have Resistance to all damage for the next minute.

You turn into a potted plant until the start of your next turn. While you're a plant, you have the Incapacitated condition and have Vulnerability to all damage. If you drop to 0 Hit Points, your pot breaks, and your form reverts.
For the next minute, you can teleport up to 20 feet as a Bonus Action on each of your turns.

You and up to three creatures you choose within 30 feet of you have the Invisible condition for 1 minute. This invisibility ends on a creature immediately after it makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell.
A spectral shield hovers near you for the next minute, granting you a +2 bonus to AC and immunity to Magic Missile.
You can take one extra action on this turn.

You cast a random spell. If the spell normally requires Concentration, it doesn't require Concentration in this case; the spell lasts for its full duration. Roll 1d10 to determine the spell: on a 1, Confusion; on a 2, Fireball; on a 3, Fog Cloud; on a 4, Fly (cast on a random creature within 60 feet of you), on a 5, Grease; on a 6, Levitate (cast on yourself); on a 7, Magic Missile (cast as a level 5 spell); on an 8, Mirror Image; on a 9, Polymorph (cast on yourself), and if you fail the saving throw, you turn into a Goat (see appendix B); on a 10, See Invisibility.
For the next minute, any flammable, nonmagical object you touch that isn't being worn or carried by another creature bursts into flame, takes 1d4 Fire damage, and is burning.
If you die within the next hour, you immediately revive as if by the Reincarnate spell.
You have the Frightened condition until the end of your next turn. The DM determines the source of your fear.
You teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
A random creature within 60 feet of you has the Poisoned condition for 1d4 hours.
You radiate Bright Light in a 30-foot radius for the next minute. Any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of you has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn.
Up to three creatures of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you take 1d10 Necrotic damage. You regain Hit Points equal to the sum of the Necrotic damage dealt.
Up to three creatures of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you take 4d10 Lightning damage.
You and all creatures within 30 feet of you have Vulnerability to Piercing damage for the next minute.

Roll 1d6 On a 1, you regain 2d10 Hit Points; on a 2, one ally of your choice within 300 feet of you regains 2d10 Hit Points; on a 3, you regain your lowest-level expended spell slot; on a 4, one ally of your choice within 300 feet of you regains their lowest-level expended spell slot; on a 5, you regain all your expended Sorcery Points; on a 6, all the effects of row 17–20 affect you simultaneously.

table.title: Airborne Encounters
rows: A gleaming Lyrandar Air Cruiser helmed by a Friendly but pompous Noble Prodigy or Lyrandar Scion
A Strider Airship with a Hostile crew of 2d4 Pirates and one Pirate Captain
2d6 Lyrandar Skyskiffs gathered for a race; the ships' pilots are Indifferent but disgruntled toward anyone who interrupts their activities
A derelict Lyrandar Air Cruiser, stranded in the sky after its engine's elemental core shattered
Two Sphinxes of Secrets, trying to figure out how the airship flies
A flock of 2d4 Perytons hiding in a cloud, waiting to ambush unsuspecting travelers
One Roc looking for food to carry to its nest

table.title: Arctic Encounters (Levels 1—4)
rows: The partially eaten carcass of a mammoth, from which 1d4 weeks of rations can be harvested.
Single-file tracks in the snow that stop abruptly
A frozen pond with a jagged hole in the ice that appears recently made
1 orc Eye of Gruumsh and 2d8 orcs

table.title: Arctic Encounters (Levels 5—10)
rows: A half-orc druid tending to an injured polar bear. If the characters assist the druid, she gives them a vial of antitoxin.
2d6 + 1 zombies aboard a galleon trapped in the ice. Searching the ship yields 2d20 days of rations.
1 bandit captain with 1 druid, 1d3 berserkers, and 2d10 + 5 bandits
1d4 hours of extreme cold (see chapter 5 of the Dungeon Master's Guide)
1 orc Eye of Gruumsh with 1d6 orogs and 2d8 + 6 orcs
A howl that echoes over the land for 1d3 minutes

table.title: Arctic Encounters (Levels 11—16)
rows: A blizzard that reduces visibility to 5 feet for 1d6 hours
A herd of 3d20 + 60 caribou (deer) moving through the snow
A mile-wide frozen lake in which preserved corpses of strange creatures can be seen
A crumbling ice castle littered with the frozen bodies of blue-skinned humanoids

table.title: Arctic Encounters (Levels 17—20)
rows: A Circular patch of black ice on the ground. The air temperature around the patch is warmer than in the surrounding area, and characters who inspect the ice find bits of machinery frozen within.
An adventurer frozen 6 feet under the ice; 50% chance the corpse has a rare magic item of the DM's choice
A 500-foot-high wall of ice that is 300 feet thick and spread across 1d4 miles
The likeness of a stern woman with long, flowing hair, carved into the side of a mountain
1 ancient white dragon with 1d3 young white dragons

name: Astral Sea Encounters

table.title: Astral Sea Encounters
rows: 1 archmage† using the astral projection spell
1 cosmic horror* (70 percent chance it is asleep)
1 githyanki knight† mounted on a young red dragon
1 githzerai zerth† being hunted by githyanki
1 neh-thalggu*† looking for a portal to the Far Realm
1 planetar† from a nearby astral dominion
Gargantuan floating crystal obelisk of mysterious origin
1 solar† watching over a dead god that drifts nearby
1 solar dragon* (your choice of young, adult, or ancient)
1d8 unicorns galloping merrily across the Astral Sea
1 spelljamming ship (roll on the Ship Encounters table)

footnotes: Creatures marked with an asterisk (*) appear in this book; the rest are described in the Monster Manual. Any creature marked with a dagger (†) can serve as a spelljammer because it is a spellcaster.

table.title: At Sea Encounters
rows: Whirlpool (25 percent chance that the whirlpool is a portal to the Elemental Plane of Water)
Passing merchant ship (galley or sailing ship)
Iceberg (easily avoided if seen from a distance)
NPC in the water (clinging to floating debris)
Sea monster (such as a dragon turtle or kraken)

table.title: Cloud Giant Encounters
rows: 1 cloud giant seeking to learn the secrets of 1 spectral cloud (attitude for both: 1d8)
1 cloud giant (attitude: 1d12) trading riddles with 1 djinni (attitude: 1d6 + 4)
1 cloud giant destiny gambler (attitude: 1d8 + 2) conferring with 1 mage (attitude: 1d12)
1d4 doppelganger spies (attitude: 1d8 + 1) posing as servants while they try to glean secrets
2 cloud giants (attitude: 1d10 + 2; roll separately for each) engaged in a wager or battle of wits
1 cloud giant of Evil Air bossing around 2 air elementals (attitude for all: 1d6)
2d4 goliath giant-kin (attitude: 1d6 + 4) trying to retrieve an owlbear (attitude: 1d6) on a rampage after running away from its giant owner
1d4 + 1 vampiric mists (attitude: 1d4 + 1) lurking in a fog bank
1 cloud giant smiling one (attitude: 1d10) seeking the Misty Vale (see chapter 4)

A momentary formation in the waves that looks like an enormous humanoid face

1 commoner singing a dirge (day only) or 1 banshee (night only)
A stoppered bottle containing an illegible note and half buried in the sand
A battle at sea between two galleons

A severed humanoid hand tangled in a net
1 sahuagin baron with 1d3 sahuagin priestesses and 2d8 sahuagin

2d6 ghasts crawling over 1d6 wrecked ships and feeding on the dead

1d6 + 2 waterspouts that dance on the water before stopping abruptly

table.title: Baldur's Gate Encounters
rows: A Mage Apprentice and their Shield Guardian seek an answer to a difficult magical puzzle.
A popular Gladiator seeks challengers to publicly demonstrate the gladiator's might.
An Assassin asks the characters pointed questions about a nearby establishment.
A Noble suggests the characters secure an invitation to a party at Eomane House (see "Blood Night" later in this chapter).
A Doppelganger merchant is offloading stolen weapons at a suspiciously low price.
2d4 Performers hold an impromptu street show while their Spy ally picks pockets.
1d3 Priest Acolytes of Oghma peddle tickets to a lecture at the Unrolling Scroll.
An old sailor suggests that the Harborhands crew at the dock needs aid (see "Tide of Teeth" later in this chapter).
A disguised Lamia bookseller and its 2d4 Jackalwere minions promise rare tomes that guarantee entry into Candlekeep.
2d4 Pirates on shore leave start a fight.
1d4 Druids rail against recent public works that have devastated a local park.
Two Cultist Fanatics devoted to Myrkul hide blanket-covered corpses in an empty shed.
A Tough Boss and 1d4 Toughs shake down a shopkeeper behind on protection payments.
2d6 Flaming Fist members (one is a Warrior Veteran, the others are Warrior Infantry) berate citizens about a recent robbery.
A merchant (Noble) specializing in Mechanical Wonders sends the characters to meet the clever clock-worker Flurn Eightspoke (see "Clockwork Memories" later in this chapter).
A Swarm of Rats surges from an alley where 1d6 Wererats wait to ambush wealthy travelers distracted by the swarm.
An Otyugh lumbers from a sewer entrance, enraged at a recent civic initiative to sluice clean water through its home.
2d4 Commoners share drinks in celebration of their crew's recent good fortune.
1d4 Nobles spill out of one of Cottle's carriages, unsure how they've suddenly arrived in such a disreputable part of town.

table.title: Calim Desert Encounters
rows: The party spots an oasis out of their way. However, the oasis is a mirage.
An Ankheg lair is buried in the sand nearby.
Light rain falls. Overnight, the desert blooms with rare flora potentially useful in crafting magic items or working high magic.
1d6 Gnoll Warriors riding Giant Hyenas seek prisoners.
A Calim sandstorm is coming! (See "Environmental Effects" earlier in this chapter.)
3d6 Bandits, led by a Bandit Captain, rob any travelers they meet. They ride Camels.
A Druid leads 2d6 Scouts on a pilgrimage.
The party stumbles on the corpses of 1d4 unfortunate travelers. The desiccated corpses rise as Mummies when night falls.
The party spots the crest of a Bulette as the creature hunts for prey.
An oasis surrounded by detailed sculptures has a masked attendant who's a Medusa.
The party spots a temple to a deity such as Chauntea, Ilmater, or Selûne. Long abandoned, it's protected by a Guardian Naga.
A Cult of the Dragon expedition including a Mage, a Death Cultist, and 2d4 Cultists are traveling to a far-off Ancient Blue Dragon who wants to become a dracolich.
A caravan bound for the nearest settlement wants to hire the party for protection.
2d4 Kochar (Scouts) make temporary camp. They are peaceful and exchange news.
Scattered bones hint at a hidden treasure vault—it's home to a Sphinx of Secrets that ambushes trespassers.
A wandering Archmage seeks forgotten lore.
An Efreeti and its attendants, an Elemental Cultist and 2d4 Cultists, camp nearby.
The party wanders into the ruins of an ancient city swallowed by the desert. It is now the lair of an Ancient Blue Dragon.
The exoskeleton of a long-dead purple worm has become a temporary shelter for 2d6 Commoners.
The city of Miziltep flies by in the distance.

table.title: Calimport Encounters
rows: Sultana Songal, in disguise as a simple scholar, asks the party for news from afar.
An Adult Gold Dragon disguised as a charismatic aristocrat seeks its stolen hoard.
Four Priest Acolytes, led by a Priest, carry the statue of a deity through the street.
A crew of 2d6 Pirates gets kicked out of a tavern and staggers drunkenly into the party.
A merchant offers exactly the magic item one of the party has been looking for.
Construction workers cry for help when the scaffolding around a nearby temple breaks, leaving them hanging above the ground.
An Archmage accompanied by 1d4 Earth Elementals rudely insists the party get out of the road and let them pass.
A Chasme flies overhead, chased by Zeraphi on Carpets of Flying.
An Assassin on a rooftop stalks a Noble.
A portal to Sigil opens in the street, and an Empyrean emerges.
A Mechanical Wonder (domestic) chases an escaped pet.
A Noble recruits the adventurers for an urgent matter that requires great discretion.
A Commoner hosts a con game in the street, challenging tourists to identify where they've hidden a (fake) jewel.
2d4 Kochar (Scouts) compete in an archery contest.
An angry genie emerges from a nearby shop. Everyone gives them a wide berth.
A Mechanical Wonder (flying) has lost its way and falls in the party's path.
A Mage using a Mechanical Wonder (mobility) barters with a merchant for rare spell components.
A gnome engineer asks the party to field-test an experimental tunneling vehicle.
Deryan Kaya instructs six aspiring inventors on the latest Mechanical Wonders.
Sultana Songal, with guards and attendants, floats through the city in a magic litter.

table.title: Cormanthor Encounters
rows: A healing spring lies in a grove sacred to elven gods. A creature that drinks from the spring regains 1d8 Hit Points but can benefit from the spring only once a day.
An abandoned animal den provides shelter.
A pack of 2d4 Wolves follows the party, ambushing the characters when they are distracted.
1d6 Goblin Warriors riding Worgs hunt for easy prey.
A Dryad observes the party. If the characters respect the forest, the dryad approaches.
Two Displacer Beasts ambush the party.
2d4 Gnoll Warriors prowl a dilapidated cabin with hidden treasure inside.
An elf Scout Captain and 2d4 Scouts patrol the forest and observe the party from hiding.
A Shambling Mound created by Moander's corruption fights any living thing it sees.
The characters enter the territory of a Primeval Owlbear. If left alone, it ignores them.
3d6 Skeletons climb from their mass grave and begin combat.
A Mage with two Warrior Veteran bodyguards search ruins for treasure. If the party looks vulnerable, they initiate combat.
The party has stumbled into the hunting ground of a Young Green Dragon.
Ancient crypts are now home to a Ghast Gravecaller and 2d6 Ghouls.
The party enters a rotten grove where a Spore of Moander grows.
A Nycaloth leads 2d4 Mezzoloths on a hunt.
A Lich and 2d4 Death Cultists search the ruins for lost magical secrets.
A Zhentarim Assassin hides from the law.
A tree warped by magic and corruption has become a Gulthias Blight.
An elf Archmage and Questing Knight are trying to recover a family heirloom.

table.title: Sea of Moonshae Encounters
rows: 2d4 Bullywug Warriors try to climb up the side of the ship and loot it of valuables.
1d4 Hunter Sharks begin following the ship.
A pod of 3d10 Killer Whales races the ship.
One of the characters spots a bottle bobbing in the sea not far from the ship. Inside is a message and a map (see "Message in a Bottle" later in this chapter).
A Noble clings to a piece of driftwood.
A Ffolk merchant vessel bound for the Sword Coast hails the characters and offers to trade.
A Norlander whaling ship approaches to ask if anyone has seen whales nearby.
The ship enters an area of Rusted Sea (see "Moonshaes Terrain").
2d4 Sahuagin Warriors riding Reef Sharks spot the ship. They follow and try to sneak aboard.
A pack of 1d4 Plesiosauruses closes on the ship and tries to sink it.
The characters spot the wreckage of a trading vessel that hit a hidden sandbar (see "Wreck of the Silverhand" later in this chapter).
A Giant Shark ambushes the ship.
The characters spot an Archelon. It ignores them unless attacked.
The ship passes an island where 1d6 Pirates led by a Pirate Captain have been left behind after a mutiny. The pirates hail the characters and pretend to be stranded travelers.
A Norlander longship crewed by fifty Guards armed with battleaxes and led by a Berserker Commander searches for a ship to capture or a coastal settlement to raid.
1d6 Frost Giants living on a passing island pelt the ship with stones.
A Storm Giant strides along the sea floor on its way to Maelstrom.
A Dragon Turtle sleeps half submerged as the ship passes. It might be mistaken for a small island.
The ship sails near the lair of a Kraken.

table.title: Ten-Towns Encounters
rows: The characters stumble on bile lichen.
A follower of Seer Echomorne insists the characters come and hear their dooms.
Three Imps from Caer-Dineval ambush the characters.
Two Zhentarim Toughs try to intimidate the characters into giving up their gold and gear.
A bloodcursed Berserker from Dougan's Hole fights the characters.
The characters discover a ritually murdered corpse, sacrificed to Auril.
A Priest of Tempus, drunk on honey mead, mistakes the characters for old enemies.
A character discovers a piece of chardalyn, through which Zlan whispers to them alone.
Twelve Frost Giants on Mammoths approach the gates, demanding the party be sent out.
Mind flayers speak through the voices of every person in town, announcing that the Great Thawing is nearly complete.

table.title: Wilderness Encounters
rows: A pack of six Wolves hunts the characters.
The characters come across a Reghed camp.
Weird lights flicker at night from the ruins of a giant settlement buried in the snow.
An earthquake shakes the ground, and a new steam vent opens at the characters' feet.
A Remorhaz begins combat with a dwarf's bones and armor stuck in its teeth.
An Elemental Cultist stalks the characters, seeking to take away their light, heat, and food.
An Adult White Dragon circles overhead.
Psychic emanations from deep under the ice trouble the character's sleep.
A group of 2d6 Toughs from the Reghed Glacier spots the characters and approaches.
A character falls through thin ice into a mind flayer colony that lies just below the surface.

table.title: Frost Giant Encounters
rows: 1 frost giant (attitude: 1d8 + 1) leading 1 titanothere (attitude: 1d10) loaded with fur and timber
1 young silver dragon (attitude: 1d10 + 3) tracking a frost giant raiding party
1 frost giant hunting with 1d4 winter wolves (attitude for all: 1d6)
2 frost giants (attitude: 1d6 + 2) burying a body that rises as 1 frostmourn (attitude: 1d4 + 1) in the process
2d4 giant goats (attitude: 1d6 + 4) wandering about with chewed tethers
1 troll (attitude: 1d10 + 2) anxiously searching for the lost goats it tends for a frost giant tribe

1 ogre bolt launcher and 1d4 + 2 ogres (attitude for all: 1d6) bringing spoils from a raid to their frost giant leader
1 frost giant everlasting one (attitude: 1d4 + 1) plotting revenge against the tribe that exiled it

1 troll mutate (attitude: 1d6) drawing, scratching, or painting with too many claws

2 ettins (attitude: 1d8) playing cards, with each head as an individual player in a four-player game

1 barrowghast and 2 zombies (attitude for all: 1d4 + 1) prowling for living creatures to slay
1 frostmourn (attitude: 1d8 + 1) contemplating the many notches on its greataxe
1d4 shadows (attitude: 1d8) playing out the last moments of their lives as a shadow puppet show on a wall
2d6 zombies (attitude: 1d4 + 1) shuffling listlessly, following a path of Giant runes painted in dried blood

table.title: Grassland Encounters (Levels 1—5)

1 gnoll pack lord with 1d4 giant hyenas
1d6 + 2 giant wasps or 1d4 + 3 swarms of insects
2d6 giant wolf spiders or 1 giant eagle
giant elk or 1 gnoll pack lord or 1d3 giant hyenas

rows: A tornado that touches down 1d6 miles away, tearing up the land for 1 mile before it dissipates
